relevance_reason: Identifies β2AR as a regulator of SNCA transcription and shows in a Norwegian population cohort that β2AR agonist and antagonist use are associated with lower and higher PD risk; adds functional work in mouse models and SNCA-triplication iPSC models.

findings.statement: Mittal et al. (2017) screened 1,126 compounds for effects on endogenous SNCA expression in human SK-N-MC neuroblastoma cells. Three of the four confirmed hits were selective beta-2-adrenoreceptor (ADRB2) agonists: metaproterenol, clenbuterol, and salbutamol. Each lowered SNCA mRNA and alpha-synuclein protein in SK-N-MC cells and in rat primary cortical neurons.
quotes: We screened 1126 compounds, including drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and a diverse set of natural products, vitamins, health supplements, and alkaloids
Unexpectedly, three of these hits were β2AR agonists (Fig. 1B), and these were prioritized for further investigation.
In rat primary cortical neurons, endogenous SNCA mRNA (Fig. 1C) and α-synuclein protein (Fig. 1D) levels were significantly, but modestly, reduced in response to β2AR activation

findings.statement: Mittal et al. (2017) found that SNCA expression changed in both directions with beta-2-adrenoreceptor activity. Snca mRNA and protein rose by 100% and 120% in primary neurons from Adrb2-knockout mice. In SK-N-MC cells, silencing ADRB2 or treating with the antagonist propranolol increased SNCA expression, and overexpressing ADRB2 reduced it. ADRB2 was required for the agonist effect on SNCA.
quotes: Endogenous Snca mRNA and α-synuclein protein levels were increased by 100 and 120%, respectively, compared with those in controls

Collectively, these internally consistent data suggest that β2AR modulation is sufficient for altering endogenous SNCA expression and necessary for mediating the effects of β2AR ligands on endogenous SNCA expression.

findings.statement: Mittal et al. (2017) showed that beta-2-adrenoreceptor ligands regulate SNCA transcription through histone 3 lysine-27 acetylation (H3K27ac) at the SNCA promoter and at 2 putative enhancers in intron 4. Clenbuterol reduced H3K27ac at these sites, and propranolol increased it. Blocking deacetylation with valproic acid abolished the agonist effect. The authors proposed that beta-2-adrenoreceptor antagonists increase SNCA expression, leading to alpha-synuclein accumulation, mitochondrial oxidative stress, and increased PD risk.
quotes: Clenbuterol treatment reduced H3K27ac across the promoter (site 1, Fig. 3A) and two putative intronic enhancers (sites 2 and 3, Fig. 3A), compared with vehicle treatment
Inhibition of H3K27 deacetylation (by cotreatment with valproic acid) abrogated the β2AR agonist effect on SNCA expression (Fig. 3C).

We propose a model in which β2AR antagonists increase SNCA expression through H3K27 acetylation, resulting in α-synuclein accumulation, mitochondrial oxidative stress, dopaminergic neurodegeneration, and increased risk of PD.

findings.statement: Mittal et al. (2017) studied the whole Norwegian population (4.6 million people) using the Norwegian Prescription Database, with 11 years of follow-up. Use of the beta-2-adrenoreceptor agonist salbutamol was associated with a reduced risk of PD (rate ratio 0.66; 95% CI, 0.58-0.76), and the reduction was dose-dependent. Use of the antagonist propranolol was associated with an increased risk (rate ratio 2.20; 95% CI, 1.62-3.00). Inhaled corticosteroids did not reduce PD risk, which the authors took as evidence against smoking fully explaining the salbutamol association. The authors noted that association does not imply causation.
quotes: Salbutamol was associated with decreased risk of PD, with a rate ratio of 0.66 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.58 to 0.76]
Propranolol was associated with a markedly increased risk of PD, with a rate ratio of 2.20 (95% CI, 1.62 to 3.00)
However, inhaled corticosteroids, which are frequently prescribed for asthma, did not reduce the PD risk (rate ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.12)

findings.statement: Mittal et al. (2017) found that intraperitoneal clenbuterol crossed the blood-brain barrier in wild-type mice and lowered alpha-synuclein protein and mRNA in the substantia nigra. Clenbuterol also prevented MPTP-induced loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons and cresyl violet-stained cells in the substantia nigra pars compacta.
quotes: β2AR activation lowered the expression of endogenous α-synuclein protein and mRNA levels in the PD vulnerable substantia nigra (P = 0.01; two-tailed Student’s t test) (Fig. 2D).
Clenbuterol treatment abrogated the MPTP-induced loss of TH+ neurons (Fig. 4, C and D) and, importantly, also blocked the loss of cresyl violet–stained cells in the SNpc

findings.statement: Mittal et al. (2017) used iPSC-derived neuronal precursor cells and neurons from a patient with autosomal dominant PD caused by SNCA locus triplication. Clenbuterol reduced SNCA mRNA and alpha-synuclein protein in these cells. Under rotenone exposure, it also reduced mitochondria-associated superoxide production and increased cell viability.
quotes: SNCA-triplication iPSC-derived neuronal precursor cells were treated with clenbuterol (20 μM), and endogenous SNCA mRNA expression and α-synuclein protein levels were significantly reduced
Clenbuterol treatment ameliorated this increased mitochondria-associated superoxide production (Fig. 4G) and increased viability (Fig. 4H), similarly to partial SNCA knockdown.

relevance_reason: Reports T-cell autoimmune responses to alpha-synuclein peptides in PD patients and links them to PD-associated HLA alleles, giving evidence about disease mechanism and HLA association. It reports no causal Mendelian variants.

findings.statement: Sulzer et al. (2017) studied 67 patients with PD and 36 age-matched healthy controls from San Diego and New York City. About one-third of the PD patients carried the HLA class II alleles DRB1*15:01/DRB5*01:01, compared with about 15% of controls (p = 0.036 and 0.022), which the authors took as showing an association of HLA-DR variants with PD in their cohort.
quotes: we recruited 67 PD participants and 36 age-matched non-PD healthy controls (HC)

While ~15% of HC carried DRB1*15:01/DRB5*01:01 alleles, ~1/3 of PD carried these alleles (difference between PD and HC, p=0.036 and 0.022 for DRB1*15:01/DRB5*01:01), indicating association of HLA DR allelic variants with PD in our cohort
findings.population: US (San Diego and New York City); predominantly Caucasian

findings.statement: Sulzer et al. (2017) stimulated peripheral blood mononuclear cells with alpha-synuclein peptides and identified 2 antigenic regions. One was near the N terminus (residues 31-46, the Y39 region), and Y39 phosphorylation was not required for the response. The other was near the C terminus (residues 116-140, the S129 region) and required phosphorylation of S129, a form present in Lewy bodies. Phosphorylated S129 epitopes produced markedly higher IL-5 responses in PD patients than in controls (p = 0.02).
quotes: We identified two antigenic regions in α-syn, the first near the N terminus, composed of aa31GKTKEGVLYVGSKTK aa45 and aa32KTKEGVLYVGSKTKE aa46 (referred to as the Y39 region)
The second antigenic region was near the C terminus (aa116–140) (referred to as the S129 region) (Fig 1a), and required phosphorylation of amino acid residue S129.
produced markedly higher IL-5 responses in PD than HC (p=0.02, Fisher’s exact test, 300 SFC threshold)

findings.statement: Sulzer et al. (2017) found that IFN-gamma and IL-5 responses to the Y39 and S129 region epitopes differed significantly between PD patients and controls. In PD patients the response was mainly IL-5 (71% IL-5 vs 29% IFN-gamma), whereas the rarer responses in controls were not polarized in this way. About 40% of PD participants had immune responses to alpha-synuclein epitopes.
quotes: were different between PD and HC for secretion of both IFNγ (two-tailed Mann-Whitney test, p<0.05) and IL-5 (two-tailed Mann-Whitney test, p<0.001)

The response was primarily polarized towards IL-5 in PD (71% IL-5 and 29% IFNγ; Fig. 2d). This polarization was PD specific, and the relatively rare HC responses were not similarly polarized (46% IL-5 and 54% IFNγ).
Approximately 40% of the PD participants in our cohort exhibited immune responses to α-syn epitopes

findings.statement: Using intracellular cytokine staining in 9 PD participants, Sulzer et al. (2017) found that about 0.2% of CD3+ T cells responded to alpha-synuclein peptides. The responses were mostly mediated by CD4+ T cells producing IL-4 or IFN-gamma; in 1 patient the response was mostly from IFN-gamma-producing CD8+ T cells. T-cell lines specific for these epitopes were also activated by antigen-presenting cells pulsed with native or fibrillized alpha-synuclein protein (in 7 of 12 and 11 of 12 cases, respectively).
quotes: Approximately 0.2% of CD3+ T cells responded to the α-syn peptides.
Thus, T cell response to α-syn antigenic peptides was largely mediated by IL-4 or IFNγ-producing CD4+ T cells, with potential contributions from CD8+/IFNγ producing T cells.
T cells lines specific for the α-syn epitopes were activated by antigen presenting cells pulsed with native or PFF protein in 7/12 and 11/12 cases

findings.statement: In in vitro binding assays, Sulzer et al. (2017) found that the PD-associated HLA class II alleles DRB1*15:01 and DRB5*01:01 bound the Y39-region epitope with high affinity (2.8 nM and 8.1 nM). C-terminal S129-region peptides bound HLA class II alleles weakly, apart from 1 peptide that bound DQB1*05:01 strongly, which the authors suggested meant these peptides are recognized promiscuously. HLA expression did not differ between PD patients with and without DRB1*15:01, suggesting that the DRB1*15:01 association with PD is not due to differential expression of the protein.
quotes: The HLA class II variants DRB1*15:01 and DRB5*01:01 bound the epitope with high affinity (2.8 nM and 8.1 nM, respectively)
Thus, antigenic peptides in the C terminus S129 antigenic region demonstrated relatively little clear restriction, suggesting that they are recognized promiscuously.
This suggests that the association between DRB1*15:01 and PD is not based on differential expression of the protein.

findings.statement: Sulzer et al. (2017) found that among PD patients, responders to the Y39 epitope more often carried DRB1*15:01 (odds ratio 4.4), DRB5*01:01 (odds ratio 3.7), DQB1*03:04 and A*11:01 than non-responders. DRB3*02:02 was negatively associated with response, suggesting it might be protective. The 4 alleles DRB1*15:01, DRB5*01:01, DQB1*03:04 and A*11:01 together accounted for every individual responding to the Y39 epitope (p = 0.00007). About half of PD patients carried one of these 4 alleles, compared with about 20% of controls (p = 0.008).
quotes: Of PD participants, 8/13 responders to the aa32KTKEGVLYVGSKTKEaa46 epitope expressed both DRB1*15:01 and DRB5*01:01, while only 12/45 (DRB1*15:01) and 13/43 (DRB5*01:01) non-responders expressed the alleles
The four alleles DRB1*15:01, DRB5*01:01, DQB1*03:04 and A*11:01 accounted for every single individual responding to the aa39 epitope (p=0.00007 for PD, Table 1).
We detected negative association between recognition of aa32KTKEGVLYVGSKTKEaa46 and the DRB3*02:02 allele, suggesting this allele might be protective.

findings.statement: Sulzer et al. (2017) found that 5 of 19 PD patients, but none of 12 controls, responded to short alpha-synuclein peptides that are candidates for MHC class I presentation. The 9-mer VLYVGSKTK (residues 37-45) bound HLA-A*11:01 with good affinity (IC50 = 161 nM), and responses to it were mostly from IFN-gamma-producing cells. The authors concluded that immune responses to alpha-synuclein in PD have both MHC class I- and class II-restricted components.
quotes: We found that 5/19 PD responded to these short peptides while 0/12 HC responded
the 9mer aa37VLYVGSKTKaa45, which is nested within the two 10mers, bound with good affinity (IC50 = 161 nM)
Thus, immune responses to α-syn associated with PD have both MHC class I and II restricted components.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study reporting a marginal association of the MC1R p.R160W variant with Parkinson disease in a Spanish population; a susceptibility locus finding relevant to the late-onset PD entry.

findings.statement: Tell-Marti et al. (2015) sequenced the entire MC1R gene in 870 Parkinson disease patients and 736 controls from Spain. They found that the MC1R melanoma risk variant p.R160W (rs1805008) was marginally associated with PD (odds ratio 2.10, gender- and age-adjusted p = 0.009, Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.063). The authors suggested that MC1R genetic variants modulate the risk of PD in the Spanish population.
quotes: sequencing the entire gene in 870 PD patients and 736 controls ascertained from Spain
We found that the MC1R variant p.R160W (rs1805008) is marginally associated with PD (odds ratio = 2.10, gender- and age-adjusted p = 0.009, Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.063).
Our results suggest that MC1R genetic variants modulate the risk of PD disease in the Spanish population.

findings.statement: Tell-Marti et al. (2015) noted that epidemiologic studies have reported co-occurrence of Parkinson disease and melanoma, which prompted their study of MC1R, a gene whose common variants are associated with melanoma, as a modifier of PD risk.
quotes: Epidemiological studies have reported the co-occurrence of Parkinson disease (PD) and melanoma.
Common genetic variants in the MC1R (melanocortin 1 receptor) gene, which determines skin and hair color, are associated with melanoma.

relevance_reason: An eQTL study in immune cells from healthy people. It found that Parkinson disease GWAS risk variants are enriched for monocyte-specific cis-eQTLs, which points to a role for myeloid cells in PD. The paper reports no patients and no causal variants.

findings.statement: Raj et al. (2014) carried out an eQTL study of purified naive CD4+ T cells and CD14+CD16- monocytes from 461 healthy individuals of European, African American, and East Asian ancestry in Boston. Susceptibility alleles for Parkinson disease and Alzheimer disease were enriched for monocyte-specific cis-eQTL effects. Alleles for autoimmune diseases such as multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis were instead enriched for T cell-specific effects. The authors suggested that the inflammatory component of susceptibility to neurodegenerative diseases may be driven more strongly by the myeloid compartment of the immune system.
quotes: On the other hand, Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), lipid traits, and type 2 diabetes susceptibility alleles are enriched in monocyte-specific effects (Fig. 3, A and B).
On the basis of these results, we suggest that the inflammatory component of susceptibility to neurodegenerative diseases may be more strongly driven by the myeloid compartment of the immune system.
Multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis are enriched in T cell effects (green), whereas Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases are enriched in monocyte effects (orange).
findings.population: European American, African American, East Asian American

findings.statement: Raj et al. (2014) noted that their study examined young, healthy individuals and so supported a role for myeloid cells in the prodromal phase of neurodegenerative diseases. They proposed that blood monocytes are likely proxies for infiltrating macrophages and/or resident microglia at the sites of neuropathology.
quotes: Because our study examines young and healthy individuals, we provide support for a role of myeloid cells in the prodromal phase of neurodegenerative diseases.
they are likely to be proxies for the infiltrating macrophages (which differentiate from monocytes) and/or resident microglia found at the sites of neuropathology.

relevance_reason: Large case-control association study testing pigmentation and melanoma GWAS SNPs for association with Parkinson disease risk. It found no significant association, which is a negative susceptibility finding relevant to the PD entry.

findings.statement: Dong et al. (2014) tested 11 SNPs from earlier genomewide association studies (GWAS) of pigmentation or melanoma in the PAGE study (808 PD cases and 1,623 controls, all non-Hispanic white). They then tested 360 such SNPs in the IPDGC dataset (5,333 PD cases and 12,019 controls). In PAGE, rs4911414 at the ASIP gene was associated with PD after Bonferroni correction (p = 0.001), but it was not associated with PD in IPDGC (p = 0.43). None of the 360 SNPs were associated with PD risk after correction for multiple comparisons. The authors concluded that GWAS SNPs for pigmentation or melanoma were not significantly associated with PD risk.
quotes: However, neither these SNPs nor pigmentation phenotypes were associated with PD risk after Bonferroni correction with the exception of rs4911414 at the ASIP gene (p = .001).

However, this SNP was not associated with PD risk in the larger dataset of IPDGC (P=0.43), and none of the other 359 SNPs selected for analysis in the IPDGC dataset showed statistical significance with PD
In conclusion, we did not find significant associations between GWAS SNPs of pigmentation or melanoma and the risk for PD.

findings.statement: Dong et al. (2014) found that MC1R rs1805007, which an earlier smaller study had associated with PD, was not significantly associated with PD in the IPDGC dataset (OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.94-1.19, P = 0.37).
quotes: In the IPDGC, rs1805007 at MC1R, the SNP that showed significant association with PD in the previous study had an OR of 1.06 (95%CI: 0.94-1.19, P=0.37).

findings.statement: In the PAGE study, Dong et al. (2014) found first primary melanoma in 18 PD cases (2.2%) and 26 controls (1.6%), giving a nonsignificant odds ratio of 1.32 (95% CI 0.71-2.44). Hair, eye, and skin color were not significantly associated with PD risk.
quotes: In the PAGE study, we identified 18 PD cases (2.2%) and 26 (1.6%) controls with first primary melanoma.
In the PAGE study, neither pigmentation phenotypes nor melanoma were statistically associated with PD risk. A modest association of melanoma and PD was suggested with an OR of 1.32 (95%CI: 0.71-2.44)

relevance_reason: Functional and chemical-genetic study of α-synuclein toxicity in yeast, worm, rat neuron and PD patient iPSC models, showing that an Rsp5/Nedd4-dependent compound rescues PD-relevant cellular pathology. It gives mechanistic and therapeutic context but reports no new patient variants.

findings.statement: Tardiff et al. (2013) found an N-aryl benzimidazole (NAB) compound in a screen of yeast cells expressing toxic levels of α-synuclein. NAB reversed several α-synuclein-induced phenotypes: vesicular α-synuclein foci, reactive oxygen species, the block in ER-to-Golgi trafficking, and protein nitration. It did not reduce α-synuclein levels.
quotes: NAB reversed diverse phenotypes caused by α–syn, including the accumulation of vesicular α-syn foci (Fig. 1C), the generation of reactive oxygen species (Fig. 1D), the block of ER-Golgi trafficking (Fig. 1E), and the nitration of proteins.
however, NAB did not reduce α-syn accumulation (Fig. 1E).

findings.statement: Tardiff et al. (2013) found that NAB reversed α-synuclein toxicity or pathology in three neuronal models: dopaminergic neuron degeneration in C. elegans expressing human α-synuclein, loss of dopaminergic neurons in rat primary cultures expressing A53T α-synuclein, and cortical neurons derived from induced pluripotent stem cells of PD patients carrying either the A53T mutation or an α-synuclein triplication. In the patient-derived neurons, both genotypes caused protein trafficking defects and nitrosative stress.
quotes: Third, we tested cortical neurons differentiated from PD-patient induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) carrying either the A53T α–syn mutation or an α-syn triplication, both of which caused protein trafficking defects and nitrosative stress.
In each case, NAB reversed α–syn toxicity or pathology, suggesting the compound’s target and mechanisms of action (MOA) were conserved from yeast to human cells

findings.statement: Tardiff et al. (2013) used chemical genetic screens in yeast to show that NAB acts through the HECT-domain E3 ubiquitin ligase Rsp5, the yeast homolog of the mammalian Nedd4 family, to promote endosomal transport. A point mutation in Rsp5 (rsp5G747E) conferred resistance to NAB2 and blocked its rescue of α-synuclein toxicity. α-Synuclein itself impaired endosomal trafficking from the plasma membrane and Golgi to the vacuole, and NAB2 restored this trafficking. The authors suggested that dysfunctional vesicle trafficking is a druggable node in α-synuclein pathology.
quotes: Three chemical genetic screens in wild-type yeast cells established that NAB promoted endosomal transport events dependent on the E3 ubiquitin ligase Rsp5/Nedd4. These same steps were perturbed by α-syn itself.
Together, these analyses established Rsp5 as the central node and only potential protein target within the NAB network.
Thus, the ability of NAB to promote Rsp5-dependent processes directly restored diverse cellular pathologies caused by α–syn, including both ER-to-Golgi and endosomal trafficking (Fig. 4D, Fig. S8).

relevance_reason: Patient iPS cell-derived cortical neurons carrying SNCA mutations (A53T, triplication) and a yeast model were used to identify early alpha-synuclein-related pathologic phenotypes (nitrosative stress, ERAD substrate accumulation, ER stress) and small-molecule/genetic rescue. Postmortem sporadic PD cortex showed the same trend. This is mechanistic evidence relevant to PD pathogenesis.

findings.statement: Chung et al. (2013) made cortical neurons from iPS cells of a female Contursi kindred patient carrying the SNCA A53T mutation and from mutation-corrected isogenic controls. They identified pathologic phenotypes in the mutant neurons that were guided by modifiers from yeast alpha-synuclein toxicity screens. These phenotypes were increased nitric oxide and nitrosative stress (nitrotyrosine), accumulation of ER forms of the ERAD substrates glucocerebrosidase (GCase) and nicastrin starting at 4 weeks, and ER stress (increased PDI and BIP, with unchanged CHOP). Increased nitrotyrosine staining and accumulation of the ER form of GCase were also seen in postmortem cortex from A53T patients.
quotes: Intraneuronal FL2 signals increased in A53T neurons relative to corrected neurons, again most readily visualized in the cell body.
ER forms of GCase and Nicastrin accumulated, and the ratio of post ER/ER forms declined in A53T compared to mutation-corrected patient neurons starting at four weeks
The increase in the ER form of GCase, and the decrease in the post-ER to ER ratio, was recapitulated in the brain of an A53T patient (fig. 3C and fig. S7B).

findings.statement: Chung et al. (2013) found that cortical neurons derived from iPS cells of a male Iowa kindred patient with SNCA triplication, who had aggressive dementia and parkinsonism, accumulated ERAD substrates and showed increased ER stress, closely phenocopying A53T neurons. Cortex from sporadic PD samples showed the same trend of ER GCase accumulation.
quotes: This patient harbored a triplication of the wild-type αSyn gene and manifested aggressive dementia in addition to parkinsonism (Table S1).
ERAD substrates accumulated (fig. 3A and fig. S6B) and ER stress increased (fig. S5C) in neurons from this patient, closely phenocopying A53T cells.
Cortex from sporadic PD samples exhibited the same trend (fig. S7).

findings.statement: In a yeast alpha-synuclein toxicity model, Chung et al. (2013) found that alpha-synuclein caused dosage-dependent protein nitration that was specific to alpha-synuclein. Raising or lowering nitric oxide by deleting COX5 isoforms increased or decreased toxicity accordingly, showing that nitrosative stress contributes to toxicity. The yeast suppressor Hrd1 and its human homolog synoviolin (SYVN1) rescued alpha-synuclein toxicity in rat cortical neurons, and SYVN1 reduced ER accumulation of GCase and nicastrin in A53T patient neurons.
quotes: Thus, in yeast, nitrosative stress is not simply a consequence of αSyn toxicity, but contributes to toxicity.
In primary rat cortical neurons lentiviral expression of Syvn1 rescued αSyn toxicity in a dose-dependent manner (fig. 3D, right).
Syvn1 also reduced nicastrin and GCase accumulation in the ER of the A53T patient cortical neurons (fig. 3E).

findings.statement: Chung et al. (2013) found that NAB2, a small molecule from a yeast screen that activates the Rsp5/Nedd4 ubiquitin ligase pathway, lowered nitric oxide levels in A53T patient neurons. It also increased the post-ER forms of nicastrin and GCase and decreased their immature forms. Lentiviral overexpression of NEDD4 had the same effect as the compound.
quotes: NAB2 reduced protein nitration in the yeast syucleinopathy model (fig. 4A) and decreased NO levels in A53T patient neurons (fig. 4B).
It increased the post-ER forms, and decreased the immature forms, of Nicastrin and GCase in PD patient neurons (fig. 4C and fig. S8).
This phenocopied the effects of the compound, increasing the mature forms of Nicastrin and GCase (fig. 4D).

relevance_reason: Reports miRNA expression changes in brains from people with idiopathic PD, plus functional studies in cells that link miR-34b/c to mitochondrial dysfunction and to reduced DJ1 and Parkin. This is pathogenesis evidence for late-onset PD.

findings.statement: Miñones-Moyano et al. (2011) profiled miRNA expression in Parkinson disease brain samples. They found decreased miR-34b and miR-34c in brain areas with variable neuropathologic involvement at clinical (motor) Braak stages 4 and 5, including the amygdala, frontal cortex, substantia nigra, and cerebellum. The miR-34b/c changes were also present at pre-motor stages (Braak stages 1-3), in cases that had received no PD-related treatment during life.
quotes: MiRNA expression profiling revealed decreased expression of miR-34b and miR-34c in brain areas with variable neuropathological affectation at clinical (motor) stages (Braak stages 4 and 5) of the disease, including the amygdala, frontal cortex, substantia nigra and cerebellum.
Furthermore, misregulation of miR-34b/c was detected in pre-motor stages (stages 1-3) of the disease, and thus in cases that did not receive any PD-related treatment during life.

findings.statement: In differentiated SH-SY5Y dopaminergic neuronal cells, Miñones-Moyano et al. (2011) found that depleting miR-34b or miR-34c moderately reduced cell viability. The depletion also altered mitochondrial function and dynamics, caused oxidative stress, and lowered total cellular ATP. Lower miR-34b/c was coupled to lower expression of DJ1 and Parkin, and both proteins were reduced in PD brain samples with strong miR-34b/c downregulation. The authors proposed that early miR-34b/c deregulation in PD triggers downstream transcriptome changes that underlie mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress.
quotes: Depletion of miR-34b or miR-34c in differentiated SH-SY5Y dopaminergic neuronal cells resulted in a moderate reduction in cell viability that was accompanied by altered mitochondrial function and dynamics, oxidative stress and reduction in total cellular adenosin triphosphate content.
MiR-34b/c downregulation was coupled to a decrease in the expression of DJ1 and Parkin, two proteins associated to familial forms of PD that also have a role in idiopathic cases.
Accordingly, DJ1 and Parkin expression was reduced in PD brain samples displaying strong miR-34b/c downregulation.

relevance_reason: Mouse model (EAAC1/Slc1a1 knockout) showing age-dependent loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons with oxidative stress, and neuroprotection by N-acetylcysteine; relevant as an animal model and therapeutic rationale for PD.

findings.statement: Berman et al. (2011) found that EAAC1 (SLC1A1)-null mice, which have impaired neuronal cysteine uptake and reduced neuronal glutathione, showed age-dependent loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, with no difference at 3 months but a 41 +/- 10% decrease by 12 months of age. Neuronal loss was accompanied by increased nitrotyrosine formation in nigral dopaminergic neurons, increased nitrosylated alpha-synuclein (primarily as dimers and higher-order aggregates), and microglial activation. Striatal dopamine and metabolites showed only nonsignificant reductions, and motor deficits were found only on the pole test at 12 months.
quotes: No differences were found at 3 months, but a significant, 41 ± 10% decrease in the EAAC1−/− brains was apparent by age 12 months (see Fig 1).
This neuronal loss was accompanied by increased nitrotyrosine formation, nitrosylated α-synuclein, and microglial activation.
Western blots of brain tissue from WT and EAAC1−/− mice confirmed a striking increase in nitrosylated α-synuclein, primarily as dimers and higher-order aggregates, in the aged EAAC1−/− mice (Fig 3C).

findings.statement: Berman et al. (2011) showed that oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC), a membrane-permeable cysteine prodrug, restored reactive thiol (glutathione) content in nigral dopaminergic neurons of EAAC1-null mice, and that long-term administration from weaning through 12 months reduced dopaminergic neuronal loss, nitrotyrosine immunoreactivity, and pole test deficits. The authors suggested that these findings provide a rationale for clinical evaluation of glutathione repletion in PD.
quotes: Dopaminergic neurons from the EAAC1−/− mice showed significantly less C5-maleimide staining than neurons from WT mice, and this reduction was reversed in EAAC1−/− mice fed NAC (Fig 5).
Brains evaluated at 12 months of age showed less dopaminergic neuronal loss in the SNc of EAAC1 mice treated with NAC (Fig 6A).
The salutary effects of N-acetylcysteine in this mouse model provide an impetus for clinical evaluation of glutathione repletion in PD.

findings.statement: Berman et al. (2011) found that EAAC1 expression was higher on dopaminergic (TH-positive) neurons than on other neurons in mouse midbrain, and that normal human brain likewise showed increased EAAC1 expression in dopaminergic neurons; in 4 postmortem PD brains, the EAAC1 signal in surviving dopaminergic neurons was at least as great as in 4 control brains. They suggested a key role for EAAC1 in dopaminergic neuronal glutathione metabolism and a contributory role for glutathione depletion in dopaminergic neuronal death.
quotes: As in the mouse brain, normal human brain showed increased EAAC1 expression in dopaminergic (TH-positive) neurons (see Fig 4B).
The EAAC1 signal in the surviving dopaminergic neurons of the PD brain sections was at least as great as in the normal brain sections
Together, these findings suggest a key role for EAAC1 in dopaminergic neuronal glutathione metabolism and a contributory role for glutathione depletion in dopaminergic neuronal death.

relevance_reason: Case-control association study of late-onset PD susceptibility loci in a Spanish cohort. It replicated the MAPT and SNCA associations and did not replicate PARK16, PARK17 or PARK18.

findings.statement: Mata et al. (2011) genotyped 7 SNPs in 1,445 Parkinson disease patients and 1,161 controls from northern Spain. Under an additive model adjusted for sex, age and site, PD was significantly associated with rs356219 in SNCA (OR 1.23; 95% CI 1.09-1.38; p = 5.5 x 10(-4)) and with rs1800547 in MAPT (OR 0.79; 95% CI 0.70-0.90; p = 3.1 x 10(-4)). In age-stratified analyses, these associations were significant only in the late-onset group.
quotes: there was a highly significant association between PD and SNPs in MAPT (rs1800547; odds ratio [OR], 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70–0.90; p = 3.1 × 10−4) and SNCA (rs356219; OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.09–1.38; p = 5.5 × 10−4)
In the age-stratified analyses, a significant association with PD was seen only for MAPT and SNCA in the late-onset group (Supplemental Table 1).

findings.statement: Mata et al. (2011) found that the A allele of MAPT rs1800547, a surrogate marker for the MAPT H1 haplotype, was associated with Parkinson disease under an adjusted dominant model in their Spanish case-control sample (OR 1.23; 95% CI 1.05-1.44; p = 1.1 x 10(-2)).
quotes: The “A” allele of rs1800547 serves as a surrogate marker for the MAPT “H1” haplotype
In our dataset, analysis of the A allele in an adjusted dominant model yielded an OR of 1.23 (95% CI, 1.05–1.44; p = 1.1 × 10−2).

findings.statement: Mata et al. (2011) did not replicate the association of Parkinson disease with PARK16 (rs823156 near SLC41A1, p = 0.09; rs947211, p = 0.50), PARK17 (GAK rs11248051, p = 0.60), PARK18 (HLA-DRA rs3129882, OR 1.01, p = 0.88) or a chromosome 8 intergenic SNP among 1,445 Spanish patients and 1,161 controls. None of these markers was associated in the overall sample or in any age stratum. The authors suggested that population structure, insufficient power (particularly for PARK16), or population-specific environmental interactions could explain the discordance with earlier GWAS. For PARK18, their sample had 99% power at the originally reported OR of 1.31.
quotes: However, none of the markers in PARK16-18 associated with Parkinson's disease in the overall sample, or in any age stratum, with P values ranging from .09 to .88.
In contrast, we failed to detect an association of this SNP with PD in our sample (OR, 1.01; p = 0.88)
Our sample provided 99% power to detect an effect at the OR reported in the original study (1.31) and 84% power at the OR observed in the combined replication sample (1.18).

relevance_reason: A pharmacogenetic trial in PD patients showing that the COMT Val158Met genotype changes how patients respond to entacapone. This is clinical management context for the PD entry.

findings.statement: In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, Corvol et al. (2011) studied 33 Parkinson disease patients who were homozygous for the COMT Val158Met polymorphism: 17 were Val/Val (high activity, COMT-HH) and 16 were Met/Met (low activity, COMT-LL). Each patient had two acute levodopa challenges, one with 200 mg entacapone and one with placebo. Entacapone increased the best ON time more in COMT-HH than in COMT-LL patients (39 +/- 10 vs 9 +/- 9 minutes, p = 0.04). It also raised levodopa AUC more (+62% vs +34%, p = 0.01) and inhibited red blood cell COMT activity more in COMT-HH patients. The authors concluded that the COMT-HH genotype enhances the effect of entacapone on levodopa pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics.
quotes: Thirty-three PD patients, homozygous for the COMT alleles COMT(HH) (n = 17) and COMT(LL) (n = 16), were randomized in a double-blind crossover trial consisting of 2 successive acute levodopa challenges associated with 200mg entacapone or placebo.
The gain in the best ON time was higher in COMT(HH) than in COMT(LL) patients (39 ± 10 vs 9 ± 9 minutes, p = 0.04, interaction between treatment and genotype).
The COMT(HH) genotype in PD patients enhances the effect of entacapone on the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of levodopa.

relevance_reason: The study reports how often known PD mutations (PRKN, LRRK2, GBA, DJ1, SNCA, PINK1) occur in 953 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease. It includes GBA and LRRK2 genotype data that bear on PD susceptibility. However, the cohort is early-onset only, not late-onset PD.

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) screened 953 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (age at onset 50 years or younger), recruited at 13 movement disorders centers without regard to family history, for mutations in SNCA, PRKN, PINK1, DJ1, LRRK2, and GBA. They found mutations in 158 (16.6%): 64 (6.7%) in PRKN, 35 (3.6%) LRRK2 G2019S, 64 (6.7%) in GBA, and 1 (0.2%) in DJ1. No carriers of the tested SNCA or PINK1 mutations were found.
quotes: One hundred fifty-eight (16.6%) participants had mutations, including 64 (6.7%) PRKN, 35 (3.6%) LRRK2 G2019S, 64 (6.7%) GBA, and 1 (0.2%) DJ1.
No carriers of the tested SNCA or PINK1 mutations were identified.

findings.statement: Among the 953 patients with early-onset PD, Alcalay et al. (2010) identified 58 GBA mutation carriers: 18 L444P heterozygotes, 38 N370S heterozygotes, and 2 N370S homozygotes. GBA mutations accounted for 40% of all mutations detected. Carriers of GBA N370S were more likely to be Jewish than non-Jewish.
quotes: Fifty eight were GBA mutation carriers: 18 L444P heterozygotes, 38 N370S heterozygotes and two N370S homozygotes.
the inclusion of GBA genotyping (which accounts for 40% of the mutations detected here)
The association was driven by LRRK2 G2019S carriers and GBA N370S carriers who were more likely to be Jewish than non-Jewish (Table 4).

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that, after adjustment for covariates, carrying GBA L444P was associated with a higher UPDRS-III motor score (worse motor performance) compared with non-carriers. They described this as the first report of a difference in motor severity between PD patients with different GBA mutations.
quotes: In a linear regression model, L444P mutation status was associated with worse motor performance, as represented in a higher UPDRS-III score (OR 7.4, 95%CI 2.0–12.8, p=0.007), after adjustment for age, gender and disease duration
this is the first report of a difference in severity of motor signs among PD cases with different GBA mutations

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) identified 31 LRRK2 G2019S carriers (30 heterozygotes and 1 homozygote) and 1 carrier of the LRRK2 G2385R variant among patients with early-onset PD. G2019S carriers were more likely to have the postural instability and gait difficulty (PIGD) motor phenotype (96%) and were more likely to be Jewish.
quotes: Thirty one were LRRK2 G2019S carriers (30 heterozygotes, one homozygote). One subject carried the LRRK2 G2385R variant; no other pathogenic LRRK2 mutations were found.
LRRK2 G2019S carriers were more likely to manifest the PIGD motor phenotype

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that 33 patients were PRKN heterozygotes and 27 carried two PRKN mutations (homozygous or compound heterozygous). PRKN carriers had an earlier age at onset and were more often Hispanic (15.6% vs 5.9%). The authors suggested that the high frequency of PRKN heterozygotes may support the idea that even a single PRKN mutation is a risk factor for early-onset PD.
quotes: 33 were PRKN heterozygotes, and 27 were PRKN homozygotes/compound heterozygotes.
Hispanics were more likely to be PRKN carriers than non-Hispanics (15.6% versus 5.9% p=0.003, Fisher exact test).
the high frequency of PRKN heterozygotes may support the notion that even a single PRKN mutation is a risk of EOPD

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that mutations were more common in early-onset PD patients with onset at age 30 or younger (40.6% vs 14.6%), in those with Jewish ancestry (32.4% vs 13.7%), and in those with a first-degree family history of PD (23.9% vs 15.1%). The family-history association was absent in Jewish patients.
quotes: Mutation carriers were more frequent among cases with AAO ≤30 than among cases with AAO between 31 and 50 (40.6% vs. 14.6% p<0.001, Fisher exact test).
Overall, mutations were more common in individuals with Jewish ancestry than in those without (32.4% versus 13.7%, p<0.001 Fisher exact test).
However, this association was much weaker in Jews, where 31.8% of those with FHPD and 32.2% of those without a FHPD carried an identified mutation

findings.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found 7 patients with early-onset PD who carried mutations in more than one gene, including LRRK2 G2019S together with GBA L444P or N370S, and PRKN heterozygous mutations together with GBA mutations. None of these patients reported PD in a first-degree relative.
quotes: Demographic and disease characteristics of seven individuals who carried more than one mutation are described in Table 2. None of these subjects reported a FHPD in a first-degree relative.

relevance_reason: GWAS identifying an HLA-DRA (rs3129882) susceptibility locus for late-onset sporadic PD, plus confirmation of SNCA, MAPT and GAK associations and their combined effects.

findings.statement: Hamza et al. (2010) performed a genome-wide association study of 2,000 Caucasian Parkinson disease patients and 1,986 controls from the NeuroGenetics Research Consortium (NGRC). They found a novel association with the HLA region on chromosome 6p21.3, with the peak at rs3129882 in intron 1 of the HLA-DRA gene (P = 2.9 x 10(-8) after adjustment for sex, age and 2 principal components). The association replicated in 2 independent datasets (meta-analysis OR 1.26, P = 1.9 x 10(-10)).
quotes: We uncovered a novel genetic association with PD in the HLA region (chromosome 6p21.3). The peak significance was at the rs3129882 polymorphism in intron 1 of HLA-DRA gene.
The association was genome-wide significance even after adjusting for four covariates (sex, age, PC1, PC2), P=2.9×10−8
We replicated association of rs3129882 in two independent data sets, (Table 1, ORMeta-analysis=1.26, PMeta-analysis=1.9×10−10).

findings.statement: Hamza et al. (2010) found that the HLA-DRA rs3129882 association was uniform across strata of family history, age at onset, sex and environmental exposures, and was particularly strong for sporadic PD (P = 5.5 x 10(-10)), late-onset PD (P = 2.4 x 10(-8)), and men (P = 1.1 x 10(-7)). There was no evidence for interaction with smoking, coffee, NSAIDs, SNCA rs356220, or MAPT rs199533.
quotes: Stratified analysis by family history, age at onset, gender and environmental exposures revealed ubiquitous associations across strata, and tests of heterogeneity across strata were not significant (Supplementary Table 2).
Associations were particularly strong for sporadic PD (P=5.5×10−10), late-onset PD (P=2.4×10−8), and men (P=1.1×10−7).

findings.statement: Hamza et al. (2010) confirmed associations of PD with SNCA (rs356220, P = 3.4 x 10(-11)) and MAPT (rs199533, P = 1.3 x 10(-6)) and replicated association with GAK on 4p16 (rs11248051; NGRC P = 3.1 x 10(-4); combined with Pankratz et al. data OR 1.46, P = 3.2 x 10(-9)). They did not replicate PARK16; 2 of 6 BST1 SNPs and 3 LRRK2 SNPs from a Japanese study reached P < 0.05.
quotes: Our GWAS confirmed the known PD-susceptibility regions at SNCA (P=3.4×10−11) and MAPT (P=1.3×10−6), as we had previously reported.

We confirmed the association of PD with cyclin G-associated kinase (GAK, 4p16, Supplementary Figure 3), as suggested by Pankratz et al. (rs11248051 PNGRC=3.1×10−4, ORNGRC+Pankratz =1.46, PNGRC+Pankratz =3.2×10−9).
We did not replicate PARK16 (ORs were in opposite direction from Satake results, P=0.03–0.15).

findings.statement: Hamza et al. (2010) examined the combined effects of SNCA, MAPT, GAK and HLA risk alleles. Compared with subjects carrying 0 or 1 risk allele, PD risk was doubled with 4 risk alleles (OR 2.49, P = 6.5 x 10(-8)) and 5-fold higher with 6 or more (OR 4.95, P = 5.5 x 10(-13)).
quotes: Compared to subjects who had one or no risk allele, the risk of PD was doubled for individuals who had four risk alleles (OR=2.49, 95%CI=1.79–3.47, P=6.5×10−8), and was five-fold higher for individuals who had six or more risk alleles (OR=4.95, 95%CI=3.20–7.64, P=5.5×10−13).

findings.statement: Using NGRC data, Hamza et al. (2010) estimated that the heritability of PD declined from 0.6 to 0.4 after excluding known pathogenic and susceptibility loci, but stayed significant, suggesting that additional unidentified genes exist.
quotes: Heritability of PD declined from 0.6 (P<0.0001) to 0.4 (P=0.01), but was still significant, suggesting additional unidentified genes exist.

findings.statement: Hamza et al. (2010) found that the frequency of the rs3129882 risk allele in controls varied significantly by region, from 0.36 in Washington to 0.46 in New York. It was low in subjects of Northern European ancestry and high in Southern Europeans, particularly Italians. Within each subpopulation, patients had a higher risk-allele frequency than controls.
quotes: The frequency of rs3129882 risk allele varied significantly in controls (P=0.0007), from 0.36 in Washington to 0.46 in New York.
Similarly, we observed a frequency gradient across Europe, low in subjects with Northern-European ancestry and high in Southern-Europeans, particularly Italians (Supplementary Table 2).
Within each subpopulation (US state, or original country) patients had a higher frequency of the HLA risk allele than controls, which supports association of HLA with PD.

findings.statement: Hamza et al. (2010) noted that previous eQTL studies had identified rs3129882 as a cis-acting regulatory variant correlated with expression of HLA-DRA, HLA-DQA2 and HLA-DRB5. They suggested that the HLA association supports a role for neuroinflammation and immunity in PD pathogenesis.
quotes: Two eQTL analyses, one using microarrays and the other RNA-seq, had identified rs3129882 as a cis-acting regulatory variation that correlated significantly (P=10−7 to 10−4) with expression levels of HLA-DRA, HLA-DQA2, and HLA-DRB5.

The evidence for genetic association with HLA, particularly when obtained from a hypothesis-free GWAS, lends strong and independent support to the involvement of neuro-inflammation and humoral immunity in PD pathogenesis.

relevance_reason: Replication case-control association study of GWAS-linked PD susceptibility loci (PARK16, PARK8/LRRK2, PARK1/SNCA, BST1) in Chinese subjects, with an Asian meta-analysis.

findings.statement: Tan et al. (2010) analyzed 13 SNPs at GWAS-linked PD loci (PARK16, PARK8, PARK1, and BST1) in 2 case-control cohorts of 1,349 ethnic Chinese subjects. They found that the PARK16, PARK8, and PARK1 loci, but not BST1, were associated with PD. PARK16 SNPs were associated with a decreased risk, and PARK1 and PARK8 SNPs with an increased risk of PD.
quotes: We conducted an analysis of 13 SNPs associated with PD GWAS-linked loci in 2 case-control cohorts comprised of 1,349 ethnic Chinese subjects.

PARK16, PARK8, and PARK1 loci but not BST1 were found to be associated with PD. PARK16 SNPs were associated with a decreased risk while PARK1 and PARK8 SNPs were associated with an increased risk of PD.

findings.statement: Tan et al. (2010) performed a pooled analysis of their Chinese cohorts and 2 Japanese replication cohorts, totaling 1,366 PD patients and 16,669 controls. It showed robust association with the PARK16, PARK8, and PARK1 loci and also with BST1. The authors reported that the strength of association was similar in Chinese and Japanese subjects.
quotes: A pooled analysis of our Chinese cohorts and 2 Japanese replication cohorts involving 1,366 subjects with PD and 16,669 controls revealed robust association with these 3 loci and also BST1.
the strength of association is similar between Chinese and Japanese subjects

findings.statement: Tan et al. (2010) observed a trend toward a stronger protective effect of PARK16 SNPs in sporadic PD than in familial cases, and in older than in younger subjects.
quotes: There was a trend toward a stronger protective effect of SNPs at the PARK16 locus in sporadic PD compared to familial cases and in older compared to younger subjects.
