relevance_reason: Case-control PET imaging study of serotonin 2A receptor binding in PD patients with visual hallucinations; relevant to clinical features/pathogenesis of PD psychosis, no genetic data.

findings.statement: Ballanger et al. (2010) used PET with the selective serotonin 2A receptor ligand setoperone F 18 in 7 nondemented PD patients with complex visual hallucinations and 7 age-matched PD patients without hallucinations. Patients with visual hallucinations showed increased serotonin 2A receptor binding in the ventral visual pathway (bilateral inferooccipital gyrus, right fusiform gyrus, and inferotemporal cortex) and in the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, medial orbitofrontal cortex, and insula. The authors suggested that serotonin 2A receptors mediate visual hallucinations in PD via the ventral visual pathway, and proposed treatment studies with selective serotonin 2A receptor antagonists.
quotes: Seven patients having PD with VHs and 7 age-matched patients having PD without VHs were recruited.

Patients having PD with VHs demonstrate increased serotonin 2A receptor binding in the ventral visual pathway (including the bilateral inferooccipital gyrus, right fusiform gyrus, and inferotemporal cortex) as well as the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, medial orbitofrontal cortex, and insula.
This pilot study provides the first in vivo evidence suggesting a role for serotonin 2A receptors in mediating VHs via the ventral visual pathway in PD.

relevance_reason: Title-only: reports a negative association of the PDXK rs2010795 variant with Parkinson disease in an Italian population; relevant to the association-studies portion of the PD entry.

findings.statement: Guella et al. (2010) found that the PDXK rs2010795 variant was not associated with Parkinson disease in an Italian population.
quotes: The PDXK rs2010795 variant is not associated with Parkinson disease in Italy.

relevance_reason: The title reports a study of whether the pyridoxal kinase gene is associated with Parkinson disease. Only the title was available, so no data could be extracted.

findings.statement: Vilariño-Güell et al. (2010) studied the association of pyridoxal kinase (PDXK) with Parkinson disease.
quotes: Association of pyridoxal kinase and Parkinson disease.

relevance_reason: Reports a risk-associated SNP in PDXK for idiopathic PD in three European cohorts, plus expression changes in substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons; this is susceptibility evidence for late-onset PD.

findings.statement: Elstner et al. (2009) identified an association between idiopathic PD and an intron 8 SNP in the PDXK gene, rs2010795. In a German cohort of 676 PD patients and 972 controls, the association was p = 3.2 x 10(-4) (OR 1.319; 95% CI 1.134-1.534). It was replicated in British (203 cases, 1,126 controls; p = 0.028; OR 1.3) and Italian (353 cases, 704 controls; p = 0.00252; OR 1.35) cohorts. In the combined analysis of 1,232 PD patients and 2,802 controls the p value was 1.18 x 10(-7) (OR 1.304; 95% CI 1.178-1.444). A second PDXK SNP in the 3-prime UTR, rs2070535, was also associated in the German cohort (p = 6.4 x 10(-4); OR 0.783).
quotes: in PDXK, two SNPs with r2 = 0.29 reached significant p values for association with disease status: rs2010795 (p = 3.2 × 10−4; odds ratio [OR], 1.319; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.134–1.534) lies in intron 8 and rs2070535 (p = 6.4 × 10−4; OR, 0.783; 95% CI, 0.681–0.901) in the 3′ untranslated region of the PDXK gene
Replication genotyping of the two lead SNPs in 203 PD and 1,126 control samples from the UK cohort confirmed the association of rs2010795 with PD (p = 0.028)
In the combined analysis of 1,232 PD and 2,802 control individuals, the association of SNP rs2010795 reached a p value of 1.18 × 10−7 (combined OR, 1.304; 95% CI, 1.178–1.444).

findings.statement: Elstner et al. (2009) carried out whole-genome expression profiling of laser-microdissected substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons from 8 PD patients and 9 controls. Four transcripts were significantly altered after Bonferroni correction: MTND2, PDXK and SRGAP3 were upregulated, and TRAPPC4 was downregulated. Upregulation of ND2 and PDXK was confirmed by real-time PCR. The mtDNA-encoded respiratory chain genes were upregulated, while 13 nuclear-encoded respiratory chain genes were downregulated.
quotes: Statistical analysis of the genome-wide expression profiles using stringent Bonferroni correction revealed four transcripts to be significantly altered between PD and control samples
Upregulation of ND2 and PDXK was confirmed by real-time analysis (ND2: +2.5-fold; PDXK: +1.8-fold).
In contrast, the 13 nuclear genes coding for different members of the five respiratory chain complexes were robustly downregulated.

findings.statement: Elstner et al. (2009) found no association between PD and tagging SNPs in TRAPPC4. They suggested that variation in PDXK might influence PD risk by altering the amount or activity of the enzyme in substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons. PDXK produces pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate, a cofactor of dopa decarboxylase.
quotes: No association was seen for tagging SNPs in the TRAPPC4 gene.
Our data is the first to indicate an effect of polymorphisms in the PDXK gene on the risk for PD, possibly by influencing enzyme amount or activity in dopaminergic neurons of the SNc.

relevance_reason: A genome-wide association study of Parkinson disease in a Japanese population. It found new susceptibility loci (PARK16 on 1q32 and BST1) and confirmed associations at SNCA and LRRK2.

findings.statement: Satake et al. (2009) performed a genome-wide association study and two replication studies in a total of 2,011 Japanese patients with Parkinson disease and 18,381 controls. They identified a new susceptibility locus on chromosome 1q32 (P = 1.52 x 10(-12)) and designated it PARK16.
quotes: we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) and two replication studies in a total of 2,011 cases and 18,381 controls from Japan
We identified a new susceptibility locus on 1q32 (P = 1.52 x 10(-12)) and designated this as PARK16

findings.statement: In the same Japanese GWAS, Satake et al. (2009) identified BST1 on chromosome 4p15 as a second new risk locus for Parkinson disease (P = 3.94 x 10(-9)).
quotes: we also identified BST1 on 4p15 as a second new risk locus (P = 3.94 x 10(-9))

findings.statement: Satake et al. (2009) found strong associations between Parkinson disease and SNCA on 4q22 (P = 7.35 x 10(-17)) and LRRK2 on 12q12 (P = 2.72 x 10(-8)) in Japanese individuals. Both genes are implicated in autosomal dominant forms of parkinsonism, and the authors concluded that autosomal dominant parkinsonism loci are involved in typical PD.
quotes: We also detected strong associations at SNCA on 4q22 (P = 7.35 x 10(-17)) and LRRK2 on 12q12 (P = 2.72 x 10(-8)), both of which are implicated in autosomal dominant forms of parkinsonism
show involvement of autosomal dominant parkinsonism loci in typical PD

findings.statement: Satake et al. (2009) compared their results with a GWAS of individuals of European ancestry. PARK16, SNCA and LRRK2 were risk loci shared by both populations, while BST1 and MAPT showed population differences. The authors suggested that population differences contribute to genetic heterogeneity in PD.
quotes: By comparing results of a GWAS performed on individuals of European ancestry, we identified PARK16, SNCA and LRRK2 as shared risk loci for PD and BST1 and MAPT as loci showing population differences
suggest that population differences contribute to genetic heterogeneity in PD

relevance_reason: GWAS establishing common-variant susceptibility loci (SNCA, MAPT, PARK16, LRRK2) for typical late-onset/sporadic PD.

findings.statement: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) performed a 2-stage genome-wide association study in individuals of European ancestry from the US, Germany, and Britain: 1,713 PD cases and 3,978 controls in stage I (463,185 SNPs), with replication in 3,361 cases and 4,573 controls. Two strong association signals were observed, at SNCA on chromosome 4q22 (rs2736990, OR = 1.23, combined P = 2.24 x 10(-16)) and at the MAPT locus on 17q21 (rs393152, OR = 0.77, P = 1.95 x 10(-16)). The authors concluded that the data demonstrated an unequivocal role for common genetic variants in the etiology of typical PD.
quotes: We performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in 1,713 individuals of European ancestry with Parkinson's disease (PD) and 3,978 controls. After replication in 3,361 cases and 4,573 controls, we observed two strong association signals
one in the gene encoding alpha-synuclein (SNCA; rs2736990, OR = 1.23, P = 2.24 x 10(-16)) and another at the MAPT locus (rs393152, OR = 0.77, P = 1.95 x 10(-16))
These data demonstrate an unequivocal role for common genetic variants in the etiology of typical PD

findings.statement: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) found that 3 of the 4 significantly associated SNCA SNPs lay in the 3-prime LD block, suggesting that the causal variant is in the 3-prime region of SNCA, possibly affecting post-transcriptional RNA processing or stability. The REP1 microsatellite risk allele was in LD with the 3-prime risk alleles (r2 = 0.365 with rs3857059), and conditional analysis indicated the REP1 association was not independent. SNCA risk SNPs in PD differed from those associated with multiple system atrophy.
quotes: The 3′ block contains three of the four significantly associated SNPs, suggesting that the causal variant is located in the 3′ region of the SNCA gene.
Analysis of REP1 genotype data in 1,774 samples from the US cohort revealed the risk allele of REP1 is in LD with the 3′ risk alleles identified here (r2=0.365 with rs3857059; supplemental figure 7A)
comparison of these data reveals disparate SNCA risk SNPs in MSA and PD

findings.statement: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) found that PD risk alleles at the MAPT locus were in LD with the H1 haplotype (r2 = 0.761 with rs393152). Expression analysis in 133 human frontal cortex samples showed that the risk allele of rs393152 was associated with higher MAPT expression and lower LRRC37A expression.
quotes: Available genotype data of the H1/H2 haplotypes in this region showed that the risk alleles of the associated SNPs are in LD with the H1 haplotype (r2=0.761 with rs393152; supplementary figure 7B).
Notably the alleles at the MAPT locus associated with increase risk of PD are associated with increased expression of MAPT in the human brain.
Notably, the allele associated with higher risk for PD, A, is associated with high levels of MAPT expression and low levels of LRRC37A expression.

findings.statement: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) replicated in Europeans a locus on chromosome 1q32 found in a Japanese GWAS, designated PARK16 (rs823128, OR = 0.66, combined P = 7.29 x 10(-8); replication cohort of 2,816 cases and 3,401 controls). The locus spans SNORA72, NUCKS1, RAB7L1, SLC41A1, and PM20D1. They failed to replicate the 4p15 (BST1) signal from the Japanese study, possibly owing to low minor allele frequency in Caucasians.
quotes: We replicated the effect of a new locus detected in the Japanese cohort (PARK16, rs823128, OR = 0.66, P = 7.29 x 10(-8))
The PARK16 locus spans 5 transcripts, SNORA72, NUCKS1, RAB7L1, SLC41A1 and PM20D1.

Although we failed to replicate the signal on chromosome 4p15, which included only one gene, BST1, the low minor allele frequency of the associated SNPs in Caucasian individuals may have affected our ability to observe association.

findings.statement: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) provided supporting evidence that common variation around LRRK2 modulates PD risk: rs1491923, 0.17 Mb upstream of LRRK2, gave a combined OR of 1.14 (P = 1.55 x 10(-5)), and the Asian cohort also showed association at this locus.
quotes: provide supporting evidence that common variation around LRRK2 modulates risk for PD (rs1491923, OR = 1.14, P = 1.55 x 10(-5))
Only one SNP, 0.17Mb upstream of LRRK2, remained associated with PD after stage II (rs1491923, p=0.01; supplementary material; Figure 2D).

findings.statement: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) suggested population-specific genetic heterogeneity in PD, because the MAPT association was absent in the Japanese cohort, whereas SNCA association was replicated across populations.
quotes: Further we describe a possible population specific genetic heterogeneity in this disorder, since the association to MAPT was absent in the Asian cohort.
Association to PD at SNCA was replicated in the Japanese GWAS, confirming this as a major risk locus across populations.

findings.statement: Simón-Sánchez et al. (2009) estimated that the combined population attributable risk of the identified loci was approximately 25%, and cautioned that these values should be interpreted carefully.
quotes: The combined population attributable risk associated with the identified loci, considering the genotypic counts of those most associated SNPs in our cohort, is approximately 25% (supplemental methods).

relevance_reason: This large multicenter case-control study shows that GBA mutations are a strong susceptibility factor for Parkinson disease in many ethnic groups. It also describes the clinical features of carriers.

findings.statement: Sidransky et al. (2009) pooled GBA genotype data from 16 centers on 4 continents, covering 5,691 patients with Parkinson disease (780 Ashkenazi Jews) and 4,898 controls (387 Ashkenazi Jews). Every center found more GBA mutations in patients than in controls. Across centers, the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio for carrying any GBA mutation was 5.43 (95% CI 3.89-7.57) after excluding the Tokyo and Norway centers. The authors concluded that GBA mutations are likely a susceptibility factor rather than a Mendelian cause of PD, and are among the most common risk factors for PD identified to date.
quotes: Genotypes and phenotypic data from a total of 5691 patients with Parkinson's disease (780 Ashkenazi Jews) and 4898 controls (387 Ashkenazi Jews) were analyzed
After excluding Tokyo and Norway, the OR was slightly attenuated (OR = 5.43, 95% CI 3.89–7.57), but heterogeneity was no longer significant

While mutations in GBA are likely to be a susceptibility factor rather than a Mendelian cause of Parkinson disease, the high frequency of mutations among ethnically diverse heterogeneous cohorts of subjects with Parkinson disease render mutations in this gene among the most common
findings.population: Multiethnic: North America, South America, Europe, Israel, Asia; including Ashkenazi Jewish

findings.statement: Sidransky et al. (2009) found that, when screening only for the GBA mutations N370S and L444P, one of the two was present in 15.3% of Ashkenazi Jewish PD patients versus 3.4% of Ashkenazi controls. In non-Ashkenazi subjects, the figures were 3.2% of patients versus 0.6% of controls. The combined Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio was 3.96 for N370S and 6.73 for L444P. N370S was especially common among Ashkenazi Jews (OR 5.62) and was not found in any Asian patient or control.
quotes: one of these two mutations were found in 15.3% of Ashkenazi Jewish patients versus 3.4% of controls, and in 3.2% of non-Ashkenazi patients versus 0.6% of controls
Mantel-Haenszel combined ORs attributable to N370S (OR = 3.96, 95% CI 2.6–6.02) and L444P (OR = 6.73, 95% CI 4.5–15.42)
N370S was particularly prevalent among Ashkenazi Jews (OR 5.62, 95%CL 3.04–10.39) and was not seen among any of the Asian patients or controls

findings.statement: Sidransky et al. (2009) found that about 20% (19.6%) of Ashkenazi Jewish PD patients carried a GBA mutation once 6 to 8 mutations were screened; 20% of the mutant alleles were neither L444P nor N370S, and the odds ratio was 6.48. In non-Ashkenazi subjects whose entire GBA coding region was sequenced, 6.9% of patients carried a mutation (OR 6.51). Among the 117 mutations identified, 54% were not N370S or L444P, so up to 46% of mutant alleles could be missed by screening only for those two. In addition, 22 of 43 subjects with L444P carried recombinant alleles that included pseudogene sequence.
quotes: Including this larger number of screened mutations increased the OR for any mutation to 6.48 (95%CL 3.78–11.09).
In patients where full sequencing was performed, the OR for any GBA mutation was 6.51 (95%CL 3.62–11.7).

The mutations identified indicate that as many as 46% of mutant alleles could be missed when focusing solely on N370S and L444P. Moreover, 22 of 43 subjects with L444P carried other pseudogene sequence and hence had recombinant alleles.

findings.statement: Sidransky et al. (2009) found that 17 PD patients, 15 of them Ashkenazi, carried two GBA mutations. Fourteen were homozygous for N370S, 2 were compound heterozygous for N370S and R496M, and 1 was compound heterozygous for N370S and V394L.
quotes: Seventeen patients (15 Ashkenazi) carried two GBA mutations. Genotype N370S/N370S was observed in fourteen, N370S/ R496M in two and N370S/V394L in one.

findings.statement: Sidransky et al. (2009) found that the common GBA variants E326K and T369M, which are not pathogenic in Gaucher disease, were not significantly associated with Parkinson disease.
quotes: Full sequencing data identified two common GBA variants, E326K and T369M which are not pathogenic in subjects with Gaucher disease. Neither demonstrated a significant association with Parkinson disease.

findings.statement: Sidransky et al. (2009) found that PD patients with GBA mutations had an earlier mean age at onset than noncarriers (54.9 vs 58.8 years; p less than 0.001). Carriers were also more likely to report a first- or second-degree relative with PD (24.0% vs 17.8%). Carriers had significantly less asymmetric onset, bradykinesia, resting tremor and rigidity, and more cognitive changes (26.3% vs 19.0%). Orthostatic blood pressure changes and postural instability did not differ between the groups.
quotes: Age at onset was found to be significantly lower among subjects with GBA mutations (p-value <0.001), with a mean age of 54.9 in subjects with GBA mutations as compared to 58.8 in subjects without.
17.8% of participants without GBA mutations reported a first or second degree relative with Parkinson disease, as compared to 24.0% of subjects with a GBA mutation (p-value =0.0057).
mutations were associated with a significantly lower frequency of asymmetric onset (p-value<0.0001), bradykinesia (p-value=0.0001), resting tremor (p-value=0.0298), and rigidity (p-value<0.0001).

phenotypes.text: earlier age at onset of parkinsonism

findings.statement: Sidransky et al. (2009) noted that two kinds of mechanism had been postulated for the link between GBA and PD. One is a gain of function through enhanced protein aggregation or lysosomal dysfunction; the other is a loss of function related to fluctuations in ceramide levels.
quotes: Both a gain of function mechanism due to enhanced protein aggregation or lysosmal dysfunction or a loss of function related to fluctuations in levels of ceramide have been postulated.

relevance_reason: A prospective cohort study finding that people with a family history of melanoma had a higher risk of Parkinson disease. This suggests the two diseases share genetic factors, but the study identifies no specific genes or variants.

findings.statement: In a prospective study of 157,036 men and women in 2 US cohorts (the Health Professionals Follow-up Study and the Nurses' Health Study), Gao et al. (2009) identified 616 incident PD cases during 14 to 20 years of follow-up. A family history of melanoma in a first-degree relative was associated with a higher risk of PD (multivariate relative risk 1.85; 95% CI 1.2-2.8; p = 0.004) after adjustment for smoking, ethnicity, caffeine intake, and other covariates. A family history of colorectal, lung, prostate, or breast cancer was not significantly associated with PD risk. The authors concluded that melanoma and PD share common genetic components.
quotes: During 14-20 years follow-up, we identified 616 incident PD cases. A family history of melanoma in a first-degree relative was associated with a higher risk of PD (multivariate relative risk = 1.85; 95% confidence interval: 1.2, 2.8; p = 0.004), after adjusting for smoking, ethnicity, caffeine intake, and other covariates.
In contrast, we did not observe significant associations between a family history of colorectal, lung, prostate, or breast cancer and PD risk.
Our findings support the notion that melanoma and Parkinson disease (PD) share common genetic components.

relevance_reason: Reports a GLUD2 gain-of-function variant (T1492G, Ser445Ala) that modifies age at onset of Parkinson disease in hemizygous males; a modifier-gene finding for the PD entry.

findings.statement: Plaitakis et al. (2010) found that a rare T1492G variant in GLUD2, an X-linked gene that encodes the brain-expressed glutamate dehydrogenase hGDH2, interacted significantly with age at PD onset in Caucasian populations. The variant results in a Ser445Ala substitution in the regulatory domain of hGDH2. Hemizygous individuals developed PD 6 to 13 years earlier than subjects with other genotypes in 2 independent Greek PD groups and 1 North American PD cohort. Female PD patients who were heterozygous for the variant did not show this effect.
quotes: we report that a rare T1492G variant in GLUD2, an X-linked gene encoding a glutamate dehydrogenase (a mitochondrial enzyme central to glutamate metabolism) that is expressed in brain (hGDH2), interacted significantly with age at PD onset in Caucasian populations

Individuals hemizygous for this GLUD2 coding change that results in substitution of Ala for Ser445 in the regulatory domain of hGDH2 developed PD 6-13 years earlier than did subjects with other genotypes in two independent Greek PD groups and one North American PD cohort.
However, this effect was not present in female PD patients who were heterozygous for the DNA change.

phenotypes.text: earlier age at onset of Parkinson disease

findings.statement: Plaitakis et al. (2010) showed that the Ser445Ala variant hGDH2 enzyme had increased basal activity that resisted GTP inhibition but was markedly sensitive to modification by estrogens. They concluded that this gain-of-function variant hastens PD onset in hemizygous subjects, probably by damaging nigral cells through increased glutamate oxidative dehydrogenation. They suggested that the lack of effect in heterozygous females could be related to estrogen modification of the overactive enzyme.
quotes: The variant enzyme, obtained by substitution of Ala for Ser445, showed an enhanced basal activity that was resistant to GTP inhibition but markedly sensitive to modification by estrogens.
Thus, a gain-of-function rare polymorphism in hGDH2 hastens the onset of PD in hemizygous subjects, probably by damaging nigral cells through enhanced glutamate oxidative dehydrogenation.
The lack of effect in female heterozygous PD patients could be related to a modification of the overactive variant enzyme by estrogens.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It is a letter to the editor (with an author reply) about pigmentation as a possible link between Parkinson disease and melanoma. It gives context only and reports no patients, variants or data.

findings.statement: In a letter, Herrero Hernández (2009) discussed pigmentation as a possible clue to understanding the link between Parkinson disease and melanoma.
quotes: Pigmentation as a clue to understanding Parkinson's disease and melanoma.

relevance_reason: Review article on Parkinson disease (abstract only); gives a general description, mentions susceptibility genes and treatment, but reports no original patients, variants or experiments.

findings.statement: In a review, Lees et al. (2009) described Parkinson disease as a common progressive bradykinetic disorder that can be accurately diagnosed. It is characterized by severe loss of nigral cells in the pars compacta and by accumulation of aggregated alpha-synuclein in specific brainstem, spinal cord and cortical regions. The authors stated that age is the main known risk factor.
quotes: Parkinson's disease is a common progressive bradykinetic disorder that can be accurately diagnosed. It is characterised by the presence of severe pars-compacta nigral-cell loss, and accumulation of aggregated alpha-synuclein in specific brain stem, spinal cord, and cortical regions.
The main known risk factor is age.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Neuronal loss in central nervous system

findings.statement: Lees et al. (2009) noted that susceptibility genes, including alpha-synuclein, LRRK2 and GBA, have shown that genetic predisposition is another important causal factor in Parkinson disease.
quotes: Susceptibility genes including alpha-synuclein, leucine rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK-2), and glucocerebrosidase (GBA) have shown that genetic predisposition is another important causal factor.

findings.statement: Lees et al. (2009) stated that dopamine replacement therapy considerably reduces motor handicap in Parkinson disease. They added that effective treatment of associated depression, pain, constipation and nighttime problems can improve quality of life, and that embryonic stem cells and gene therapy are promising approaches still under research.
quotes: Dopamine replacement therapy considerably reduces motor handicap, and effective treatment of associated depression, pain, constipation, and nocturnal difficulties can improve quality of life.
Embryonic stem cells and gene therapy are promising research therapeutic approaches.

relevance_reason: The title says the paper compares the phenotype of Parkinson disease patients with severe versus mild GBA mutations. That is genotype-phenotype evidence for GBA-associated PD, but only the title was available.

findings.statement: Gan-Or et al. (2009) reported a differential phenotype in Parkinson disease patients carrying severe versus mild GBA mutations.
quotes: Differential phenotype in Parkinson's disease patients with severe versus mild GBA mutations.

relevance_reason: Genotype-phenotype study of initial PD symptoms in Ashkenazi carriers of LRRK2 G2019S and GBA mutations; adds phenotypic modifier evidence for PD susceptibility genes.

findings.statement: Gan-Or et al. (2010) screened 600 Ashkenazi Jewish patients with Parkinson disease for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation and for 8 GBA mutations, and compared reported initial symptoms among GBA mutation carriers, LRRK2 G2019S carriers, and noncarriers. More LRRK2 G2019S carriers reported muscle stiffness (rigidity; p = 0.007) and balance disturbances (p = 0.008) as initial symptoms, whereas more GBA mutation carriers reported slowness (bradykinesia; p = 0.021). The authors suggested that LRRK2 and GBA mutations have distinct effects on the initial symptoms of PD.
quotes: An extended cohort of 600 Ashkenazi PD patients was screened for the LRRK2 G2019S and for eight GBA mutations.
More LRRK2 G2019S carriers reported muscle stiffness (rigidity, p = 0.007) and balance disturbances (p = 0.008), while more GBA mutation carriers reported slowness (bradykinesia, p = 0.021).
These results suggest distinct effects of LRRK2 or GBA mutations on the initial symptoms of PD.

relevance_reason: Genome-wide linkage screen in familial PD identifying susceptibility loci on 18q11 and 3q25; mapping evidence for late-onset PD.

findings.statement: Gao et al. (2009) conducted a genome-wide linkage screen of 5,824 SNPs in 278 families of European, non-Hispanic descent with Parkinson disease. Using parametric and nonparametric linkage analyses allowing for genetic heterogeneity, they found significant evidence for linkage on chromosome 18q11 (maximum lod score = 4.1) and suggestive evidence for linkage on chromosome 3q25 (maximum lod score = 2.5).
quotes: We conducted a genome-wide linkage screen of 5824 single-nucleotide polymorphisms in 278 families of European, non-Hispanic descent to localize regions that harbor susceptibility loci for PD.
Significant evidence for linkage was detected on chromosome 18q11 (maximum lod score [MLOD] = 4.1) and suggestive evidence for linkage was obtained on chromosome 3q25 (MLOD = 2.5).

findings.statement: Gao et al. (2009) found that the linkage results on 18q11 and 3q25 were strongest in families not previously screened for linkage, and simulation studies suggested that these findings were likely due to locus heterogeneity rather than random statistical error.
quotes: These results were strongest in families not previously screened for linkage, and simulation studies suggest that these findings are likely due to locus heterogeneity rather than random statistical error.

relevance_reason: Case-control study showing GBA mutations are a risk factor for Parkinson disease in British patients, with clinical and neuropathological characterisation of carriers.

findings.statement: Neumann et al. (2009) screened the GBA gene in 790 British patients with Parkinson disease and 257 controls matched for age and ethnicity. GBA mutations were found in 33 of 790 patients (4.18%) and 3 of 257 controls (1.17%), a significant difference (P = 0.01; odds ratio 3.7; 95% CI 1.12-12.14). Fourteen different GBA mutations were identified, including 3 previously undescribed ones, K7E, D443N, and G193E.
quotes: We utilized the DNA of 790 patients and 257 controls, matched for age and ethnicity, to screen for mutations within the GBA gene.

The frequency of GBA mutations among the British patients (33/790 = 4.18%) was significantly higher (P = 0.01; odds ratio = 3.7; 95% confidence interval = 1.12-12.14) when compared to the control group (3/257 = 1.17%).
Fourteen different GBA mutations were identified, including three previously undescribed mutations, K7E, D443N and G193E.

findings.statement: Neumann et al. (2009) found that Parkinson disease patients carrying GBA mutations had early disease onset, hallucinations in 45% (14 of 31), and symptoms of cognitive decline or dementia in 48% (15 of 31).
quotes: Clinical features comprised an early onset of the disease, the presence of hallucinations in 45% (14/31) and symptoms of cognitive decline or dementia in 48% (15/31) of patients.

findings.statement: Neumann et al. (2009) found on neuropathologic examination widespread and abundant alpha-synuclein pathology in all 17 GBA mutation carriers studied, graded Braak stage 5-6, with McKeith limbic or diffuse neocortical Lewy body-type pathology. Diffuse neocortical Lewy body-type pathology tended to be more frequent in GBA mutation carriers than in matched Parkinson disease controls without GBA mutations.
quotes: Pathological examination revealed widespread and abundant alpha-synuclein pathology in all 17 GBA mutation carriers, which were graded as Braak stage of 5-6, and had McKeith's limbic or diffuse neocortical Lewy body-type pathology.
Diffuse neocortical Lewy body-type pathology tended to occur more frequently in the group with GBA mutations compared to matched Parkinson's disease controls.

findings.statement: Neumann et al. (2009) concluded that GBA mutations were found in British Parkinson disease patients at a higher frequency than any other known Parkinson disease gene, and suggested that GBA mutations are a significant risk factor and, to date, the most common genetic factor identified for the disease.
quotes: This study demonstrates that GBA mutations are found in British subjects at a higher frequency than any other known Parkinson's disease gene.

strengthens the hypothesis that GBA mutations represent a significant risk factor for the development of Parkinson's disease and suggest that to date, this is the most common genetic factor identified for the disease.

relevance_reason: Prospective cohort and nested case-control study reporting association of hair color and MC1R Arg151Cys homozygosity with PD risk; susceptibility/risk factor evidence.

findings.statement: Gao et al. (2009) examined natural hair color in early adulthood and PD risk among 38,641 men (Health Professionals Follow-up Study) and 93,661 women (Nurses' Health Study) in the US, documenting 539 PD cases over 16-22 years of follow-up. PD risk increased with decreasing darkness of hair color; after adjustment for age, smoking, ethnicity and other covariates, pooled relative risks were 1, 1.40, 1.61, and 1.93 (95% CI 1.08-3.43) for black, brown, blond, and red hair, respectively. The association was particularly strong for PD onset before age 70 years (RR for red vs black hair 3.83), but not significant for onset at 70 years or older.
quotes: PD risk increased with decreasing darkness of hair color. Pooled RRs for PD were 1 (reference), 1.40, 1.61, and 1.93 (95% confidence interval, 1.1-3.4) for black, brown, blond, and red hair, respectively, after adjusting for age, smoking, ethnicity, and other covariates.
The associations between hair color and PD were particularly strong for relative younger onset of PD (<70 yr) (adjusted RR for red vs black hair = 3.83; 95% confidence interval, 1.7-8.7).
In contrast, hair color was not significantly associated with risk of PD onset at 70+ years.

findings.statement: In a case-control study nested within the HPFS and NHS cohorts (272 PD cases and 1,185 matched controls genotyped), Gao et al. (2009) found that homozygosity for the loss-of-function MC1R Arg151Cys polymorphism, which was strongly associated with red hair (RR 57), was associated with increased PD risk relative to Arg/Arg (adjusted RR 3.15; 95% CI 1.06-9.37); heterozygotes had RR 1.23. Participants with red hair who were Cys/Cys homozygotes had an RR of 4.9 compared with non-red-haired noncarriers. The authors suggested a potential role of pigmentation in PD, which may in part explain the co-occurrence of PD and melanoma.
quotes: In the case-control study, participants with Cys/Cys genotype, which was associated with red hair, had a greater PD risk, relative to the Arg/Arg genotype (adjusted RR, 3.15; 95% confidence interval, 1.1-9.4).

Participants with red hair plus carrying Cys/Cys variant were more than four times (RR=4.9, 95% CI: 1.5, 16.2) more likely to have PD relative to those who did not have red hair and did not carry the Cys allele (Table 3).
Our findings suggest a potential important role of pigmentation or ethnicity in PD, and may in part explain the higher than expected co-occurrence of PD and melanoma.

relevance_reason: This genomewide association study of familial Parkinson disease found suggestive susceptibility loci (GAK/DGKQ on 4p) and supporting evidence for association with SNCA and MAPT. No result reached genomewide significance.

findings.statement: Pankratz et al. (2009) performed a genomewide association study in familial Parkinson disease, genotyping 857 familial PD cases and 867 controls, mostly Caucasian and non-Hispanic, on the Illumina HumanCNV370Duo array. They used logistic models under additive and recessive modes adjusted for gender and age. No result met genomewide significance by Bonferroni correction. The strongest association was with SNPs in the GAK/DGKQ region on chromosome 4p (rs11248060; additive model p = 3.4 x 10(-6), OR = 1.69), and meta-analysis with a previous case-control GWAS (Fung et al.) improved this to p = 2.5 x 10(-7).
quotes: Genotyping was performed with the Illumina HumanCNV370Duo array in 857 familial PD cases and 867 controls.
The strongest association result was with SNPs in the GAK/DGKQ region on chromosome 4 (additive model: p = 3.4 x 10(-6); OR = 1.69).
Meta-analysis was performed using data from a previous case-control GWAS, and yielded improved p values for several regions, including GAK/DGKQ (additive model: p = 2.5 x 10(-7))

findings.statement: Pankratz et al. (2009) suggested that GAK was a promising candidate in the 4p region because a previous expression study had found it among 137 genes differentially expressed in PD, with a 1.56-fold change in substantia nigra pars compacta. SNPs in TMEM175, which lies between GAK and DGKQ, showed no suggestive association.
quotes: GAK is a particularly promising candidate because it is one of 137 genes shown to be differentially expressed in PD, with a 1.56-fold change in expression in the substantia nigra pars compacta of PD patients as compared to controls.
There is another gene (TMEM175) in between GAK and DGKQ; however, while there were SNPs genotyped in this gene, none showed suggestive evidence of association with PD (Fig. 3a).

findings.statement: Pankratz et al. (2009) found consistent evidence of association between familial PD and the SNCA region on chromosome 4q (additive model p = 5.5 x 10(-5), OR = 1.35 for the rs356229 minor allele). The associated SNPs lay in intron 4 and the 3-prime region of SNCA. rs356229 showed modest linkage disequilibrium with rs356219, a SNP previously associated with SNCA mRNA levels.
quotes: Consistent evidence of association was also observed to the chromosomal regions containing SNCA (additive model: p = 5.5 x 10(-5); OR = 1.35)
The rs356229 SNP that we report with a minor allele increasing risk of PD (OR = 1.35) exhibits modest LD with rs356219 (HapMap CEPH D′ = 0.65, r2 = 0.39).

findings.statement: Pankratz et al. (2009) found association with the C17orf69/MAPT region on chromosome 17 under a recessive model (rs1724425; p = 2.0 x 10(-5), OR = 0.56), which improved to p = 9.8 x 10(-6) on meta-analysis. Minor alleles tagging the protective H2 haplotype also featured in the additive meta-analysis. The authors concluded that the data supported the existing hypothesis that the complex genomic region around MAPT is related to PD risk.
quotes: MAPT (recessive model: p = 2.0 x 10(-5); OR = 0.56)
the MAPT region (recessive model: p = 9.8 x 10(-6); additive model: p = 4.8 x 10(-5))
Nonetheless, both the primary GWA analysis and meta-analysis support the existing hypothesis that the complex genomic region around MAPT is related to PD risk.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It is a correspondence about genotyping strategies for glucocerebrosidase (GBA) mutations in Parkinson disease cohorts, which bears on GBA as a risk factor for PD.

findings.statement: Gutti et al. (2008) emphasized the need for appropriate genotyping strategies for glucocerebrosidase (GBA) mutations in cohorts with Parkinson disease.
quotes: The need for appropriate genotyping strategies for glucocerebrosidase mutations in cohorts with Parkinson disease.

relevance_reason: This paper reports how often GBA and LRRK2 mutations occur in Ashkenazi Jewish patients with Parkinson disease. It also shows how GBA mutation severity relates to PD risk and age at onset, which makes it a susceptibility study for this entry.

findings.statement: Gan-Or et al. (2008) screened an Israeli Ashkenazi Jewish cohort of 420 PD patients, 333 elderly controls, and 3,805 young controls for 8 GBA mutations. Two of these mutations are associated with mild Gaucher disease (N370S, R496H) and six with severe Gaucher disease (84GG, IVS2+1, V394L, D409H, L444P, RecTL). GBA carrier frequency was 17.9% in PD patients, compared with 4.2% in elderly controls and 6.35% in young controls.
quotes: An Israeli Ashkenazi cohort of 420 patients with PD, 333 elderly controls, and 3,805 young controls was screened for eight GBA mutations, which are associated with mild (N370S, R496H) and severe (84GG, IVS2 + 1, V394L, D409H, L444P, RecTL) Gaucher disease.
GBA carrier frequency was 17.9% in patients with PD compared to 4.2% in elderly and 6.35% in young controls.

findings.statement: Gan-Or et al. (2008) found that 29% of GBA carriers among PD patients carried a severe Gaucher disease mutation, compared with 7% of GBA carriers among young controls. Severe GBA mutations increased the risk of PD 13.6-fold and mild mutations 2.2-fold. Mean age at PD onset was 55.7 years with severe mutations and 57.9 years with mild mutations, compared with 60.7 years in patients without known GBA or LRRK2 mutations.
quotes: The proportion of severe mutation carriers among PD patient GBA carriers was 29% compared to 7% among young controls.

Severe and mild GBA mutations increased the risk of developing PD by 13.6- and 2.2-fold, and affected the average age at PD onset (AAO), 55.7 and 57.9 years, compared to 60.7 years in patients without known GBA or LRRK2 mutations.

phenotypes.text: earlier age at onset of Parkinson disease

findings.statement: Gan-Or et al. (2008) also genotyped the PD patients and elderly controls for LRRK2 G2019S. PD patients carrying LRRK2 G2019S had an earlier age at onset. More than one-third of the PD patients carried a mutation in GBA or LRRK2.
quotes: Patients with PD and elderly controls were also genotyped for LRRK2 G2019S.
Additionally, an earlier AAO was observed in LRRK2 G2019S carrier PD patients.
Finally, these data demonstrate that a surprisingly high frequency, more than one third of our patient population, carried a mutation in GBA or LRRK2.

phenotypes.text: earlier age at onset of Parkinson disease

relevance_reason: Case-control study showing GBA heterozygous mutations are a susceptibility factor for PD and DLB.

findings.statement: In a case-control study of 721 patients with PD, 57 patients with dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and 554 healthy controls from 4 movement disorder clinics in the Seattle, Washington, area, Mata et al. (2008) genotyped the 2 most common GBA mutations, N370S and L444P. Heterozygote frequency was significantly higher in PD patients (2.9%; P less than 0.001) and DLB patients (3.5%; P = 0.045) than in controls (0.4%). The authors suggested that GBA mutations exert a large effect on susceptibility to Lewy body disorders at the individual level but are associated with a modest (approximately 3%) population-attributable risk in individuals of European ancestry.
quotes: Seven hundred twenty-one patients with PD, 554 healthy control subjects, and 57 patients with DLB.
We observed a significantly higher heterozygote frequency for the 2 mutations in patients with PD (2.9%; P <.001) and those with DLB (3.5%; P = .045) compared with control subjects (0.4%).

Our findings suggest that GBA mutations exert a large effect on susceptibility for Lewy body disorders at the individual level but are associated with a modest (approximately 3%) population-attributable risk in individuals of European ancestry.

relevance_reason: Case-control study of caffeine intake, CYP1A2 genotype and risk of PD. It adds gene-environment evidence on susceptibility to PD.

findings.statement: In a case-control study of 418 PD patients and 468 race-, sex- and age-matched controls, Tan et al. (2007) found no association between the CYP1A2 -163C>A polymorphism (rs762551) and PD (P = 0.08). This variant is associated with high CYP1A2 inducibility, which makes carriers fast caffeine metabolizers.
quotes: A polymorphic variant of CYP1A2 (-163C>A) (rs762551) is associated with high CYP1A2 inducibility.
886 consisting of 418 PD and 468 race, sex and age matched controls were included. No evidence existed to suggest any association between CYP1A2 and the onset of PD (P=0.08).

findings.statement: Tan et al. (2007) found that caffeine intake was significantly and inversely associated with PD (P = 2.01 x 10(-5)). Compared with low drinkers, the odds ratio was 0.71 (95% CI 0.50-1.00) for moderate drinkers and 0.47 (95% CI 0.34-0.65) for high drinkers. Multivariate analysis showed no interaction between caffeine and CYP1A2 genotype (P = 0.956). The authors concluded that the protective association was similar in fast and slow metabolizers, which supports animal evidence that both caffeine and its metabolite paraxanthine are neuroprotective.
quotes: A significant association was seen between caffeine intake and the onset of PD (P=2.01x10(-5)), with the odds ratio for moderate and high drinkers at 0.71 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.50-1.00] and 0.47 (95% CI: 0.34-0.65), respectively against the low drinkers.
Multivariate analysis revealed no evidence of any interaction effects of caffeine with CYP1A2 (P=0.956).

The association between caffeine intake and risk of PD was similarly observed in both fast and slow caffeine metabolizers, supporting experimental evidence in animal models that both caffeine and its major metabolite, paraxanthine, are neuroprotective.

relevance_reason: Title only: the paper looks at glucocerebrosidase (GBA) mutations as a risk factor for Parkinson disease in Chinese patients. That is relevant to susceptibility to late-onset PD, but no results are available.

findings.statement: Tan et al. (2007) studied glucocerebrosidase (GBA) mutations and the risk of Parkinson disease in Chinese patients.
quotes: Glucocerebrosidase mutations and risk of Parkinson disease in Chinese patients.

relevance_reason: Functional and animal-model study showing that SIRT2 inhibition rescues alpha-synuclein toxicity in cellular and Drosophila models of Parkinson disease. It gives mechanistic and therapeutic context but reports no patients or variants.

findings.statement: Outeiro et al. (2007) identified a potent inhibitor of sirtuin 2 (SIRT2) and found that inhibiting SIRT2 rescued alpha-synuclein toxicity and changed inclusion morphology in a cellular model of Parkinson disease. Genetic inhibition of SIRT2 with small interfering RNA also rescued alpha-synuclein toxicity. The inhibitors protected against dopaminergic cell death both in vitro and in a Drosophila model of Parkinson disease. The authors suggested that the results point to a link between neurodegeneration and aging.
quotes: We identified a potent inhibitor of sirtuin 2 (SIRT2) and found that inhibition of SIRT2 rescued alpha-synuclein toxicity and modified inclusion morphology in a cellular model of Parkinson's disease.
Genetic inhibition of SIRT2 via small interfering RNA similarly rescued alpha-synuclein toxicity.
Furthermore, the inhibitors protected against dopaminergic cell death both in vitro and in a Drosophila model of Parkinson's disease. The results suggest a link between neurodegeneration and aging.

relevance_reason: Mouse model and functional study of how Parkinson's disease damages dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra, plus a possible neuroprotective strategy (blocking Cav1.3 channels). No patients or variants.

findings.statement: Chan et al. (2007) suggested that dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta rely unusually on L-type Cav1.3 calcium channels to drive their maintained, rhythmic pacemaking, and that this reliance makes them vulnerable to stressors thought to contribute to Parkinson disease progression. In mice, this reliance increased with age: juvenile neurons used pacemaking mechanisms common to neurons not affected in Parkinson disease, and these mechanisms remained latent in adulthood.
quotes: Our studies suggest that the unusual reliance of these neurons on L-type Ca(v)1.3 Ca2+ channels to drive their maintained, rhythmic pacemaking renders them vulnerable to stressors thought to contribute to disease progression.

The reliance on these channels increases with age, as juvenile dopamine-containing neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta use pacemaking mechanisms common to neurons not affected in Parkinson's disease.

findings.statement: Chan et al. (2007) found that blocking Cav1.3 calcium channels in adult mouse substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons made them revert to the juvenile form of pacemaking. This 'rejuvenation' protected the neurons in both in vitro and in vivo mouse models of Parkinson disease, which the authors suggested points to a new strategy that could slow or stop disease progression.
quotes: blocking Ca(v)1.3 Ca2+ channels in adult neurons induces a reversion to the juvenile form of pacemaking.
Such blocking ('rejuvenation') protects these neurons in both in vitro and in vivo models of Parkinson's disease, pointing to a new strategy that could slow or stop the progression of the disease.

relevance_reason: Epidemiologic cross-sectional study of skin cancer and precancerous lesions in PD patients; an associated-feature finding for the PD entry.

findings.statement: In a cross-sectional survey, Ferreira et al. (2007) had a movement disorder specialist and a dermatologist examine 150 patients with Parkinson disease and 146 age-matched controls. Neoplastic or preneoplastic skin lesions were present in 35 PD patients (23.3%) and 20 controls (13.7%) (OR 1.92; 95% CI 1.05-3.51). The difference was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for sex, because controls were matched only for age and the PD group had more males. Twenty-nine PD patients (19%) had actinic keratosis and 4 (3%) had basal cell carcinoma. The authors called their results nonconclusive but said they agreed with previous studies suggesting an increased risk of skin cancer in PD.
quotes: 150 PD patients and 146 controls were included. Thirty-five PD patients (23.3%) presented skin lesions that could be classified as neoplastic or preneoplastic vs. 20 subjects in the control group (13.7%) (OR 95%, CI 1.92 [1.05, 3.51]).
However, this difference lost statistical significance when adjusted for gender (recruitment of controls was matched just for age with an over representation of males in the PD group).
Twenty-nine PD patients (19%) presented actinic keratosis and basal cell carcinoma was diagnosed in 4 patients (3%).

relevance_reason: Epidemiological data showing a higher-than-expected incidence of malignant melanoma in a cohort of patients with early Parkinson disease, with no link to levodopa; relevant to associated features.

findings.statement: Constantinescu et al. (2007) found 5 cases of malignant melanoma in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort of patients with early Parkinson disease. In a standard healthy population, 1.5 cases would be expected. The standardized event ratio was 3.3 (95% CI, 1.1-7.8), which showed a higher-than-expected incidence of melanoma. The authors found no association between levodopa therapy and melanoma incidence.
quotes: We identified all known cases of malignant melanoma (N = 5) in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort and compared that to published expected values (N = 1.5) for a standard healthy population.
The standardized event ratio was 3.3 (95% confidence interval, 1.1-7.8), indicating that incidence of malignant melanoma was higher than expected.
We found no association between levodopa therapy and the incidence of melanoma.

relevance_reason: Case-control study of clinical risk factors for dopaminergic drug-related pathological gambling in idiopathic PD; describes a treatment-related complication relevant to clinical features/management.

findings.statement: Voon et al. (2007) compared 21 patients with idiopathic PD who developed pathological gambling after starting medication with 42 consecutive PD patients without compulsive behaviors. Patients with pathological gambling had younger age at PD onset, higher novelty seeking, medication-induced hypomania or mania, impaired planning, and a personal or immediate family history of alcohol use disorders. Novelty seeking, alcohol use disorder history, and younger age at onset predicted pathological gambling with 83.7% accuracy in a logistic regression model, and the authors concluded that such patients may have a greater risk for pathological gambling with dopamine agonists.
quotes: Patients with PG had a younger age at PD onset (P = .006), higher novelty seeking (P<.001), medication-induced hypomania or mania (P = .001), impaired planning (P = .002), or a personal or immediate family history of alcohol use disorders (P = .002).
Novelty seeking, a personal or immediate family history of alcohol use disorders, and younger age at PD onset accurately predicted PG at 83.7% in a logistic regression model
Patients with PD having a younger age at PD onset, higher novelty seeking traits, and a personal or family history of alcohol use disorders may have a greater risk for PG with dopamine agonists.

relevance_reason: Mouse models of Parkinson disease showing loss of indirect-pathway eCB-LTD and rescue of LTD and motor deficits by D2 agonist plus endocannabinoid degradation inhibitors; relevant to animal model and pathogenesis.

findings.statement: Kreitzer and Malenka (2007) found that in striatum, excitatory synapses onto indirect-pathway medium spiny neurons (MSNs) had higher release probability and larger NMDA receptor currents than direct-pathway synapses. Only indirect-pathway MSNs showed endocannabinoid-mediated long-term depression (eCB-LTD), and this LTD needed dopamine D2 receptor activation.
quotes: excitatory synapses onto indirect-pathway medium spiny neurons (MSNs) exhibit higher release probability and larger N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor currents than direct-pathway synapses
indirect-pathway MSNs selectively express endocannabinoid-mediated long-term depression (eCB-LTD), which requires dopamine D2 receptor activation

findings.statement: In models of Parkinson disease, Kreitzer and Malenka (2007) found that indirect-pathway eCB-LTD was absent. A D2 receptor agonist or inhibitors of endocannabinoid degradation restored it. Giving these drugs together in vivo reduced parkinsonian motor deficits. The authors suggested that endocannabinoid-mediated depression of indirect-pathway synapses plays a critical role in controlling movement.
quotes: In models of Parkinson's disease, indirect-pathway eCB-LTD is absent but is rescued by a D2 receptor agonist or inhibitors of endocannabinoid degradation.

Administration of these drugs together in vivo reduces parkinsonian motor deficits, suggesting that endocannabinoid-mediated depression of indirect-pathway synapses has a critical role in the control of movement.

relevance_reason: Functional and animal-model study of alpha-synuclein toxicity mechanism (ER-Golgi trafficking block) and Rab1 rescue in PD models; relevant to pathogenesis/animal model sections of PD entry.

findings.statement: Cooper et al. (2006) found that in yeast the earliest defect following alpha-synuclein expression was a block in endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-to-Golgi vesicular trafficking. In a genomewide screen, the largest class of toxicity modifiers were proteins functioning at this same step, including the Rab GTPase Ypt1p, which associated with cytoplasmic alpha-synuclein inclusions.
quotes: The earliest defect following alphaSyn expression in yeast was a block in endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-to-Golgi vesicular trafficking.

In a genomewide screen, the largest class of toxicity modifiers were proteins functioning at this same step, including the Rab guanosine triphosphatase Ypt1p, which associated with cytoplasmic alphaSyn inclusions.

findings.statement: Cooper et al. (2006) showed that elevated expression of Rab1, the mammalian homolog of yeast YPT1, protected against alpha-synuclein-induced dopaminergic neuron loss in animal models of PD. The authors suggested that synucleinopathies may result from disruptions in basic cellular functions that interface with the unique biology of particular neurons to make them especially vulnerable.
quotes: Elevated expression of Rab1, the mammalian YPT1 homolog, protected against alphaSyn-induced dopaminergic neuron loss in animal models of PD.
Thus, synucleinopathies may result from disruptions in basic cellular functions that interface with the unique biology of particular neurons to make them especially vulnerable.

relevance_reason: The abstract covers APP promoter mutations in early-onset Alzheimer disease (Belgian and Dutch series). It does not mention Parkinson disease, its genes or its phenotype, so nothing in it could be cited in the late-onset Parkinson disease entry.
Only the title is available. It points to a historical review of early descriptions of Parkinson disease in ancient China, which could support a history note in the entry.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2006) reviewed early descriptions of Parkinson disease in ancient China.
quotes: Early descriptions of Parkinson disease in ancient China.

relevance_reason: Review abstract about mitochondrial dysfunction in PD pathogenesis; no patients, variants, or primary data.

findings.statement: In a review, Muqit et al. (2006) noted that impairment of mitochondrial function is thought to play a major role in the pathogenesis of Parkinson disease, and that recent genetic advances suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction may be the primary defect. They suggested that drugs targeting mitochondria may represent the best hope for disease-modifying therapies.
quotes: Impairment in mitochondrial dysfunction is thought to play a major role in the pathogenesis.
Recent genetic advances suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction may be the primary defect.
Drugs that target the mitochondria may therefore represent the best hope for disease-modifying therapies in Parkinson disease.

relevance_reason: The paper is mainly about Reelin in Alzheimer disease. For Parkinson disease it reports only that the 180-kDa Reelin band in CSF was increased, along with several other neurodegenerative disorders.

findings.statement: Botella-López et al. (2006) found that the 180-kDa Reelin band in cerebrospinal fluid was increased in all the neurodegenerative disorders they studied, including Parkinson disease, frontotemporal dementia, progressive supranuclear palsy, and Alzheimer disease. Levels of 180-kDa Reelin correlated positively with CSF Tau protein. The authors suggested that Reelin is involved in the pathogenesis of a number of neurodegenerative diseases.
quotes: Next, we examined whether CSF Reelin levels were also altered in neurological diseases, including frontotemporal dementia, progressive supranuclear palsy, and Parkinson's disease. The Reelin 180-kDa band increased in all of the neurodegenerative disorders analyzed.
Moreover, the 180-kDa Reelin levels correlated positively with Tau protein in CSF.

relevance_reason: Case-control study of GBA N370S and L444P as susceptibility factors for PD in Norway; negative association result relevant to the PD entry's heterogeneity/susceptibility discussion.

findings.statement: Toft et al. (2006) screened 311 Norwegian patients with Parkinson disease and 474 controls for 2 common functional GBA mutations, N370S and L444P. Seven patients (2.3%) and 8 controls (1.7%) carried a mutant GBA allele (p = 0.58). The authors concluded that their study did not indicate increased susceptibility to PD in GBA mutation carriers in Norway.
quotes: The authors screened a series of 311 Norwegian patients with PD and 474 controls for 2 common functional mutations of the GBA protein, N370S and L444P.
Seven patients (2.3%) and 8 controls (1.7%) carried a mutant GBA allele (p = 0.58).
This study does not indicate increased susceptibility to PD in GBA mutations carriers in Norway.

relevance_reason: An in vivo SPECT imaging study that found fewer nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in patients with Parkinson disease. This is clinical and pathophysiologic detail that supports the PD entry.

findings.statement: Fujita et al. (2006) used SPECT with the ligand [123I]5-IA to image nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in 10 nondemented Parkinson disease patients and 15 age-matched healthy controls. Compared with controls, the patients had a widespread, significant decrease of about 10% in total distribution volume in both cortical and subcortical regions, with no significant change in delivery (K1). The authors said the results indicated the importance of extending the study to demented patients.
quotes: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors were imaged in 10 nondemented Parkinson's disease patients and 15 age-matched healthy subjects using a single-photon emission computed tomography ligand
Parkinson's disease showed a widespread significant decrease (approximately 10%) of V in both cortical and subcortical regions without a significant change in K(1).

phenotypes.text: decreased cortical and subcortical nicotinic acetylcholine receptor binding

relevance_reason: Association study of GSK3B functional polymorphisms with PD risk and their interaction with MAPT haplotypes; a susceptibility modifier, not a Mendelian cause.

findings.statement: Kwok et al. (2005) identified 2 functional SNPs in the GSK3B gene. In vitro, the T allele of the promoter SNP rs334558 had greater transcriptional activity. The intronic SNP rs6438552 regulated the choice of splice acceptor site in vitro, and its T allele was associated with altered splicing in lymphocytes and higher levels of GSK3B transcripts lacking exons 9 and 11 (GSK-delta-exon9+11). Higher levels of this transcript correlated with increased phosphorylation of its substrate, tau.
quotes: A promoter single nucleotide polymorphism (rs334558) is associated with transcriptional strength in vitro in which the T allele has greater activity.
The T allele is associated with altered splicing in lymphocytes and increased levels of GSK3B transcripts that lack exons 9 and 11 (GSKDeltaexon9+11).
Increased levels of GSKDeltaexon9+11 correlated with enhanced phosphorylation of its substrate, Tau.

findings.statement: Kwok et al. (2005) found that the T allele of rs6438552 was more frequent in PD brains than in control brains. PD brains also had correspondingly higher levels of the GSK-delta-exon9+11 transcript and more tau phosphorylation.
quotes: In a comparison of PD and control brains, there was increased in frequency of T allele (rs6438552) and corresponding increase in GSKDeltaexon9+11 and Tau phosphorylation in PD brains.

findings.statement: Using conditional logistic regression, Kwok et al. (2005) found a gene-gene interaction between the T/T genotype of GSK3B rs334558 and the H1/H1 haplotype of MAPT (p = 0.009). After stratifying by tau haplotype, a GSK3B haplotype carrying the T allele at both SNPs was associated with PD risk. The odds ratio was 1.64 in H1/H2 and H2/H2 individuals (p = 0.007) and 0.68 in H1/H1 individuals (p less than 0.001). The authors suggested that GSK3B polymorphisms interact with tau haplotypes to modify PD risk.
quotes: Conditional logistic regression indicated gene-gene interaction between T/T genotype of rs334558 and H1/H1 haplotype of microtubule-associated protein Tau (MAPT) gene (p = 0.009).

There was association between a haplotype (T alleles of both GSK3B polymorphisms) and disease risk after stratification by Tau haplotypes ((H1/H2+H2/H2 individuals: odds ratio, 1.64; p = 0.007; (H1/H1 individuals: odds ratio, 0.68; p < 0.001).

relevance_reason: Whole-genome association study of PD that found SNP associations in SEMA5A and at the PARK11 and PARK10 late-onset PD susceptibility loci.

findings.statement: Maraganore et al. (2005) carried out a two-tiered whole-genome association study of Parkinson disease. In tier 1 they genotyped 198,345 SNPs in 443 sibling pairs discordant for PD. In tier 2a they genotyped 1,793 PD-associated SNPs in 332 matched case-unrelated control pairs. Eleven SNPs were associated with PD (P<.01) in both tiers with the same direction of effect, and the lowest combined P value (P = 7.62 x 10(-6)) was for a SNP within the semaphorin 5A gene (SEMA5A). The authors noted that SEMA5A plays a role in neurogenesis and neuronal apoptosis, which is consistent with existing hypotheses of PD pathogenesis.
quotes: For tier 1, we individually genotyped 198,345 uniformly spaced and informative single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 443 sibling pairs discordant for PD.
We identified 11 SNPs that were associated with PD (P<.01) in both tier 1 and tier 2 samples and had the same direction of effect.
A SNP within the semaphorin 5A gene (SEMA5A) had the lowest combined P value (P=7.62 x 10(-6)).

findings.statement: In the whole-genome association study by Maraganore et al. (2005), a second SNP among the top associations tagged the PARK11 late-onset PD susceptibility locus (P = 1.70 x 10(-5)).
quotes: A second SNP tagged the PARK11 late-onset PD susceptibility locus (P=1.70 x 10(-5)).

findings.statement: In tier 2b, Maraganore et al. (2005) genotyped 941 SNPs that were borderline significant in tier 1 (P<.05) and that tested a priori hypotheses about PD susceptibility. In the combined tier 1 and tier 2b data, the 2 SNPs with the lowest P values (P = 9.07 x 10(-6) and P = 2.96 x 10(-5)) tagged the PARK10 late-onset PD susceptibility locus. The authors said that independent replication across populations was needed.
quotes: In tier 2b, we also selected for genotyping additional SNPs that were borderline significant (P<.05) in tier 1 but that tested a priori biological and genetic hypotheses regarding susceptibility to PD (n=941 SNPs).
the two SNPs with the lowest P values (P=9.07 x 10(-6); P=2.96 x 10(-5)) tagged the PARK10 late-onset PD susceptibility locus.
